docs.title: Dividend alert! Last day to buy Asian Paints, Coal India and 6 more stocks for dividend payout worth nearl
docs.text:
Around six companies have fixed Wednesday as the record date for their respective dividends, effectively making today the last day for interested investors to buy the shares of the companies to be eligible for the dividend payouts.
 Under Sebi’s T+1 settlement cycle, investors need to purchase a company’s shares at least one trading day before the record date to ensure the shares are credited to their demat accounts in time, and they become eligible for the corporate action. Accordingly, today is the last opportunity for investors to buy the shares so that they are credited to their accounts by the record date (November 4), making them eligible for the dividend.
 Asian Paints dividend
Earlier last month, Asian Paints declared an interim dividend of Rs 5.75 per share of Re 1 face value for FY27, with November 4 (Wednesday) set as the record date to determine eligible shareholders.
The said dividend will be paid by November 13 (Friday) to those shareholders who own the shares as on the record date. The stock has a dividend yield of 1.17%, according to data on Trendlyne.
 Also read | Asian Paints Q2 Results: Net profit rises 7% YoY to Rs 1,068 crore; firm announces Rs 5.75/share dividend 
 Live Events
 Coal India dividend
 Coal India accounts for the highest dividend payout among all the stocks turning ex-record date for dividends tomorrow. The company has fixed Wednesday as the record date for its second interim dividend of Rs 10.25 apiece for the financial year 2027.
The said dividend will be paid to the eligible shareholders on or before November 27. The company has declared 36 dividends since 2011, and the stock has a dividend yield of more than 6.5%.
 Also read | Diwali stock picks: SBI Securities lists 11 stocks with up to 22% upside potential. Do you own any? 
 Other dividend stocks
 Godrej Consumer Products will pay an interim dividend of Rs 5 per share to its shareholders. The company has declared 84 dividends since October 30 and the stock has a dividend yield of nearly 2.5%.
 Privi Speciality Chemicals will also pay an interim dividend of Rs 5 per share, while Symphony will pay an interim dividend of Rs 2 per share. Other stocks with Wednesday as the record date for dividends include Vaibhav Global (Rs 1.5 per share), Praruh Technologies (Rs 1 per share) and Silver Touch Technologies (Rs 0.1 per share).

docs.title: Bonus issue alert! Last day to buy this Rakesh Jhunjhunwala-backed smallcap pharma stock for 1:1 bonus bon
docs.text:
Smallcap pharma firm Concord Biotech , which was backed by late ace investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala , has fixed November 4 (Wednesday) as the record date for its 1:1 bonus issue , making today the last day for investors to buy the stock and become eligible for the bonus shares.
 Only those shareholders who hold Concord Biotech shares in their demat accounts as of Wednesday will be eligible to receive the bonus shares. As per Sebi's T+1 settlement cycle, investors must buy the company's shares at least one trading day before the record date for them to be credited to their demat accounts and qualify for the bonus issue. This makes today the last day to buy the stock to be eligible for the bonus shares.
 Also read | Bonus issues, stock splits, dividends: Infosys, Asian Paints among over 40 stocks turning ex-date this week 
 All about Concord Biotech’s bonus issue
Concord Biotech announced in September that its board of directors considered and approved the issuance of bonus shares in the ratio of 1:1 by capitalising the company’s share premium account. The company would issue 10.46 crore bonus shares with a face value of Re 1 each as part of the corporate action.
Later in October, Concord Biotech fixed November 4 as the record date for the purpose of determining the eligibility of shareholders set to receive the bonus shares, which will be allotted by November 5 (Thursday).
 Live Events
A bonus issue consists of free shares distributed by a company from its reserves and is often seen as a sign of strong financial health and growth prospects. While the issue of bonus shares increases the total number of outstanding shares, it does not change the company’s market capitalisation. However, it can improve liquidity and affordability, allowing more investors to add shares of the company to their portfolio. A 1:1 bonus issue means that eligible shareholders will get one bonus share for every single share held in the company as on the record date.
 Also read | Diwali 2026: 77 stocks knock down D-St bears to deliver multibagger returns of up to 4,700% in a year 
 Rakesh Jhunjhunwala's investment in Concord Biotech
Ace investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala, often called India's Warren Buffet, first invested in Concord Biotech in 2004 and later helped the company's founder in buying back the company from pharma major Mylan in 2009. His investment firm RARE Enterprises stayed invested in the company during its Rs 1,551 crore IPO in 2023.
The son of an income tax officer, Jhunjhunwala started making his mark on Dalal Street in 1985, when the BSE Sensex was young, at a mere 150 level. Starting his career with a humble Rs 5,000, Jhunjhunwala built a multi-billion dollar portfolio on Dalal Street. A qualified Chartered Accountant, he invested in both his own name and his wife, Rekha Jhunjhunwala. He favoured stocks in the finance, tech, retail and pharma sectors.
He passed away at the age of 62 on August 14, 2022, following a cardiac arrest. He was suffering from multiple health problems related to the heart, diabetes and kidney, according to sources.
Rakesh Jhunjhunwala and associates held around 24% stake in Concord Biotech as of the end of the September quarter of FY27, according to data on Trendlyne.
 Also read | Bitcoin rattled by biggest crypto heist in history! Why Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger hated cryptocurrency 
 Concord Biotech share price
Concord Biotech shares have fallen more than 11% in one week and over 15% in one month, with the stock overall being down nearly 13% in 2026 so far.
The shares of the company have dropped 19% in the past one year, but delivered positive returns of a little over 3% in three years. It has a market capitalisation of around Rs 12,172 crore.

docs.title: Jio Platforms shares climb over 3% after Q2 PAT rises 14% YoY to Rs 8,389 crore. Buy, sell or hold?
docs.text:
Shares of newly listed Jio Platforms rallied as much as 3.1% to their day’s high of Rs 1,476 on the BSE on Monday after reporting a 14% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 8,389 crore in its September quarter results, marking its first earnings announcement since its stock market debut earlier in the week. The growth was supported by healthy subscriber additions, expansion in its digital services business and a marginal rise in average revenue per user (ARPU).
 Revenue from operations climbed 11% YoY to Rs 40,475 crore from Rs 36,332 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. On a sequential basis, net profit rose 8% from Rs 7,765 crore reported in the June quarter, while revenue grew 3%.
EBITDA rose 17% YoY during the quarter, supported by revenue growth, operating leverage and margin improvement. The EBITDA margin expanded 250 basis points to 54.1%. ARPU also edged higher to Rs 218.8 in the second quarter, as promotional offers for fixed broadband customers offset the benefits from a better subscriber mix and higher usage.
The results come after Jio Platforms' stock market debut on October 28. Its shares listed at Rs 1,358, representing a 21.36% premium over the issue price of Rs 1,119.
On the operational front, per capita data consumption stood at 44.2 GB per month, while total data traffic increased 22% YoY in the September quarter. Monthly subscriber churn remained stable at 1.6%, and the company added 9.1 million net subscribers during the quarter.
 Live Events
As of the end of September, Jio's 5G subscriber base stood at 300 million, an addition of 66 million users over the past 12 months. Customer engagement remained strong, with 5G accounting for 56% of total wireless traffic.
The company's fixed broadband subscriber base reached 30 million, following additions of 7.3 million customers over the last 12 months. Jio AirFiber had a total subscriber base of 15.1 million and accounted for more than 75% of Jio's fixed broadband additions during the same period.
"We warmly welcome our new shareholders to the Jio Platforms family as we enter a new era as a listed company. This quarter’s results continue to reflect the strength of our 5G network, and the growing reach of our broadband and digital services," said Akash M Ambani, MD of Jio Platforms.
He said Jio's early investments in next-generation technologies had helped establish the foundation for its success over the past decade. The company will continue to strengthen its capabilities in satellite communications, 6G intellectual property and artificial intelligence embedded in core voice and data services, he added.
 Buy, sell or hold Jio Platforms share?
Japanese brokerage Nomura was the first to initiate coverage on Jio Platforms following its stock market listing, assigning a Buy rating with a target price of Rs 1,340 from the IPO price. The stock has already crossed this target. Nomura said Jio's extensive 5G coverage has helped drive data consumption per subscriber to 27% above Bharti Airtel 's levels.
It also highlighted Jio's industry-low monthly churn rate of 1.6%, which positions the company to narrow its average revenue per user (ARPU) gap with Airtel. The brokerage summed up its assessment by saying that "the disruptor is now the leader of the industry".
Nomura expects Jio Platforms to become debt-free by FY29. The company's net debt-to-equity ratio, including deferred payment obligations, declined to 0.37 times in FY26 from 0.56 times in FY24.
Domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal also has a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 1,350, describing the company as the 'Gateway to Digital India'. According to its estimates, Jio is valued at par with Bharti Airtel's India business at both the IPO price and the current market price (CMP), excluding Indus and Bharti Airtel's minority interests.
Motilal Oswal believes Jio could command a premium over Bharti Airtel's India business in the near term, supported by its market leadership, greater influence over industry tariffs and a free float of less than 3%. However, the brokerage noted that its earnings and valuation estimates remain highly sensitive to wireless ARPU growth.

docs.title: NTPC shares rise 3% after Q2 results. Why Jefferies and Nuvama remain bullish
docs.text:
Shares of NTPC jumped over 3% to Rs 328 on the BSE in Monday’s early session after the state-owned power utility major reported a 14% year-on-year (YoY) increase in standalone net profit to Rs 5,320 crore for the July-September quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027, with brokerages maintaining their ‘Buy’ calls for the stock.
 The company’s revenue from operations meanwhile increased nearly 17% YoY to Rs 45,752 crore during the second quarter of FY27, from Rs 39,165 crore in the year-ago period. Its EBITDA rose around 9% YoY to Rs 10,891 crore during the quarter under review.
Along with the Q2 results, NTPC announced a first interim dividend of Rs 3 per share. The company has fixed November 6 as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders set to receive the dividend.
 Also read | NTPC Q2 Results: Standalone profit rises 14% YoY to Rs 5,320 crore; revenue up 17% 
The group's capital expenditure stood at Rs 23,932 crore in H1 FY27, compared with Rs 23,115 crore in the corresponding period of FY26. NTPC Group's gross fixed assets increased to Rs 4,85,444 crore as of September 30, 2026, from Rs 4,37,142 crore a year earlier.
 Live Events
 Jefferies on NTPC share price
Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ call on the shares of NTPC with a target price of Rs 425 apiece, implying 34% upside potential. The international brokerage noted that the company’s September quarter profit was 16% above its estimates, aided by lower disincentives, prompting it to raise the company’s FY27 EPS estimate by 1%.
NTPC’s management reduced FY27E RE addition guidance to 5 GW from 7-8 GW due to transmission delays, Jefferies noted, adding that the company added 1.3 GW RE capacity in the first half of FY27 and another 3.5 GW is expected in the ongoing second half of the financial year. The international brokerage lowered FY27 overall addition estimate to 6 GW from 8.2 GW which is reflected in a 1% tweak to its FY28-29 earnings estimates.
 Nuvama on NTPC share price
Nuvama Institutional Equities maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the shares of NTPC with a target price of Rs 400 apiece. The brokerage noted that strong power demand resulted in healthy PLFs YoY, leading to 11% YoY rise in SA generation.
Movement in regulatory deferral accounts rose 23% YoY. Q2 core RoE is 19.5% (+515 bps YoY) as regulated equity was down 1.6% YoY, Nuvama said, adding that efficiency gains also drove Q1 core RoE to 19.9% (+325bp YoY).
 NTPC share price
 NTPC shares have jumped more than 5% in a week but overall recorded marginal gains in a month. The shares of the company are however down nearly 6% in 2026 so far and more than 6% in the past one year.
In the longer term, NTPC shares have delivered positive returns of more than 34% in three years and 131% in five years. The company has a market capitalisation of nearly Rs 1.5 lakh crore.

 Shares of Reliance Industries (RIL) rallied nearly 12% on Monday, with the stock recording the sharpest single-day surge since April 2020, after the Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate’s Q2 earnings impressed Dalal Street investors.
 Reliance Industries’ sharp gains added nearly Rs 2 lakh crore to the total market capitalisation of India’s most valuable company, pushing it closer to Rs 17.6 lakh crore. The company's shares jumped to Rs 1,300 apiece on the NSE, the highest level seen by the stock since early September this year.
This comes after the oil-to-chemicals conglomerate reported a 41% year-on-year (YoY) rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 25,548 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 18,165 crore in the year-ago period. Its revenue from operations meanwhile increased 29% YoY to Rs 3.32 lakh crore during the quarter under review, up from Rs 2.58 lakh crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.
International brokerages including Jefferies, Nomura and others maintained their ‘Buy’ ratings on the shares of Reliance Industries following the earnings print. Jefferies has a target price of Rs 1,710 apiece, implying an upside potential of 47%. It raised the company’s FY27 and FY28 EBITDA estimates by 6% and 2%, respectively, and sees earnings upgrades and a recovery in retail growth to the mid-teens as possible catalysts for a re-rating of the stock.
 Also read | Reliance Industries shares rally 6% after Q2 results. Here’s why Jefferies, others analysts see up to 47% upside 
 Live Events
Nomura reduced its target price for Reliance Industries shares to Rs 1,560 apiece, which still implies a strong upside potential of 34%. The international brokerage noted RIL’s consolidated EBITDA came in 9% above its estimate, largely driven by stronger-than-expected performance in the oil-to-chemicals (O2C) segment, while the upstream and telecom businesses performed in line with expectations, although the retail segment missed estimates.
 Reliance Industries share price 
Notably, Reliance Industries shares have remained largely subdued in recent months, hitting a 52-week low of Rs 1,152 apiece earlier this month. The stock has declined nearly 21% so far in 2026, underperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen 11% over the same period. On a one-year basis, RIL shares are down 16%.
The stock has also shown a muted response to recent quarterly earnings announcements. Over the past five quarters, RIL shares fell after three results announcements and rose after two. The sharpest gain came on July 17, 2026, when the stock advanced 2.59%, while its steepest decline was recorded on April 24, 2026, when it fell 1.15%.
 Also read | Why is the market rallying today? 
Today’s sharp gains have helped Reliance Industries shares record more than a 4% rise in a week and 7% in a month.

 Shares of Bank of Baroda jumped nearly 5% on Monday after the lender reported a 36% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 6,532 crore for the second quarter of the financial year 2027, led by one-time gains from the sale of some of its stake in the National Stock Exchange (NSE) during its initial public offering (IPO).
 Bank of Baroda’s net profit jumped from Rs 4,809 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. It earned Rs 1,340 crore from selling a partial stake in NSE last month. The bank’s net interest income meanwhile rose 9% YoY to Rs 13,026 crore during the quarter under review. The company's shares rose to Rs 250 apiece on Monday morning.
The profit growth was aided by non-interest income almost doubling to Rs 6,881 crore during Q2 FY27, from Rs 3,515 crore in the year-ago period. Net interest margin, however, dropped to 2.74% from 2.96% a year earlier.
 Also read | Bank of Baroda Q2 profit jumps 36% to Rs 6,532 crore on NSE stake sale 
 Nomura on Bank of Baroda share price
 Nomura maintained its ‘Neutral’ rating on Bank of Baroda shares but reduced its target price to Rs 270 apiece from Rs 280. The latest target price implies 13% upside potential.
 Live Events
The brokerage said Bank of Baroda reported strong Q2 numbers, with the net profit beating its estimate by 12%. The NII was also 4% higher than Nomura’s estimate. The company’s management raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 13-15% and deposit growth guidance to 11-13%. It retained NIM guidance of 2.75-2.95%, and expects to reach the upper end in Q3 and Q4 as the repo rate hike passes through to the 38% repo-linked book.
Nomura raised FY27 and FY28 EPS estimates by 14% and 5% respectively on higher treasury income and lower provisions in FY27 and higher NII in FY28, and now builds in FY27 loan growth of 16%. It expects RoA of 0.9% and RoE of 13-14% over FY27-28.
 Systematix on Bank of Baroda share price
 Systematix Institutional Equities maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the shares of Bank of Baroda with a target price of Rs 285 apiece. The domestic brokerage said the company’s net profit was nearly 28% above its estimate.
Asset quality remained robust, as annualised gross slippage ratio improved by 18 bps QoQ to 0.8%. The GNPA and NNPA ratios improved by 21 bps and 13 bps QoQ, respectively. The bank reported operating profit of Rs 114.3 billion, supported by gains from the NSE stake sale and revaluation, the brokerage pointed out.
 Dolat Capital on Bank of Baroda share price
 Dolat Capital maintained its ‘Reduce’ rating on Bank of Baroda stock with a target price of Rs 260 apiece, implying 9% upside potential. The domestic brokerage said the company’s profit was in line with estimates.
Despite factoring in higher NIMs post rate hike, they are lower than peers, Dolat Capital said. This, coupled with the impact of upcoming provisions from ECL norms, means the brokerage expects ROAs to remain at 0.9% levels. Further, its loan growth projections of 12% over FY27 and FY28 are lower than banking system growth expectations.
 Also read | Bank of Baroda’s FCNR(B) deposits surge nearly sixfold to Rs 1.03 lakh crore 
 Bank of Baroda share price
Bank of Baroda shares have gained around 3% in one week and more than 3% in a month. Shares of the lender have, however, fallen nearly 21% in 2026 so far, as multiple headwinds impacted financial stocks.
The stock is down more than 14% in the past one year. In the longer term, Bank of Baroda shares have jumped 19% in three years and delivered multibagger returns of more than 133% in five years.

docs.title: Rise in NPA is transitory, as borrowers take time to adjust to new rules, says Muthoot Finance MD
docs.text:
KOLKATA: India's largest gold loan company Muthoot Finance said that the rise in bad loans is an outcome of the structural changes in lending rules and is not a reflection of stress.
 "Borrowers will take a little while to understand the new structure. This does not signify any stress in the industry," managing director Alexander George Muthoot said.
"It is only a transition phase where people have to just get used to this kind of a new way of servicing the loan which was not there in the past. The payment will be regularised over a few quarters," he added.
Muthoot reported a sharp rise in its gross non-performing assets ratio to 3.87% at the end of September from 2.28% three months prior.
Among other non-bank lenders, Bajaj Finance reported rise in stage 2 and 3 assets to 2.02% from 1.87% three months back and attributed this to the transitional phase while saying that it won't impact its credit cost. Shriram Finance too saw its gross stage 3 gold loan assets rising to 3.12% from 2.57% over the same period.
 Live Events
The Reserve Bank of India told lenders across the spectrum to switch to equated monthly instalments or interest only monthly payments if loans are given for more than 12 months. Bullet repayment loans where principal and interest are paid in lump sum at the end of the tenure are capped for a maximum one year period. No automatic rollover of loans is possible anymore for loans up to one year maturity. The new rules became effective from April 1.
"It's too early to make an assessment on the new regulation. Let's see how things progress, probably it will lead to better credit discipline," said Muthoot's new MD, who assumed the leadership role on October 1.
He highlighted that the company maintains an average loan to value ratio at 65% and therefore the lender always has the buffer in case the borrowers fail to repay after a certain time.
"If we have to remove NPAs, we can easily auction this gold, recover our principal and interest. But we always ensure that we use auctions as a last resort when everything else fails. About 98% of our customers pay their interest on time," the MD said.
Meanwhile, taking the advantage of easy branch opening norms, Muthoot with 5230 branches across India has accelerated the pace of physical expansion. It opened 262 branches in the first six month of the fiscal and plans to add a similar count by the end of March.
RBI said that large gold-loan companies do not need to take prior approval before opening new branches.
It had 204 ton of pledged gold at the end of September, up from 196 ton six month prior. Its assets under management grew 42% year-on-year to Rs 1.88 lakh crore, of which gold loan was Rs 1.79 lakh crore.
Indians are estimated to have monetised 1500-2000 tons of gold while a Morgan Stanley report in 2025 estimated the total household wealth in gold at around 34,600 ton.

docs.title: Tata Sons infuses ₹1,100 crore into Tata Electronics: Report
docs.text:
NEW DELHI: Tata Sons has infused ₹1,100 crore into Tata Electronics , its Apple iPhone and semiconductor manufacturing business, Moneycontrol reported recently, citing company's filings. 
This latest infusion in September follows an investment of ₹1,500 crore in March, the filings indicated. The fresh capital will fund ongoing capital expenditure in semiconductor businesses. 
 The funding aligns with Tata Electronics combining a fast-growing smartphone manufacturing business with investments in semiconductor fabrication, assembly, and testing. Tata Electronics' revenue increased 97 per cent to ₹1.31 lakh crore in FY26 from ₹66,601 crore a year earlier. 
 This growth made it the fourth-largest group company by revenue within four years of its establishment. The company reached break-even at the operating profit level, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran said in his FY26 address to shareholders. 
 However, its net loss widened to ₹1,611 crore from ₹70 crore a year earlier. Tata Sons invested ₹3,000 crore directly in the company in FY26, taking the carrying value of its investment to ₹9,961 crore at the end of that year, according to the company’s annual report. 
Tata Electronics has expanded its manufacturing footprint through the purchase of Wistron’s India n operations and a controlling interest in Pegatron Technology India. 
 Its semiconductor plans include a fabrication plant at Dholera in Gujarat, being developed with Taiwan’s Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation . This project has an announced investment outlay of ₹91,000 crore and a planned capacity of 50,000 wafers a month. 
The chips from this plant are intended for applications across automotive, computing, data storage, wireless communications, and artificial intelligence markets. The company has also announced a ₹27,000-crore semiconductor assembly and testing facility in Assam ’s Jagiroad. 
 Assembly and testing involves packaging chips made at fabrication plants and checking them before use in finished products. The two projects together carry an announced investment outlay of ₹1.18 lakh crore, spanning different stages of chip production. 
 Chandrasekaran has positioned the electronics business as a long-term investment in India’s manufacturing capabilities. He stated in his shareholder address that the semiconductor push required sustained funding, international partnerships, skilled engineers, and the development of suppliers and research collaborations.

docs.title: Himadri Speciality Chemical’s H1FY27 profit jumps 29%
docs.text:
Himadri Speciality Chemical is pairing sharp revenue growth with an ambitious industrial pivot, even as rising costs and heavier working capital needs weigh on cash generation. According to scanx.trade , the company’s latest half-year update shows a business that is still benefiting from strong demand in carbon materials, while simultaneously pushing hard into battery materials , carbon nanotubes and other higher-value products. 
 Half-year profit rises faster than costs, but cash remains tight 
For the first half of FY27, consolidated net profit increased 29 per cent year on year to ₹460 crore, supported by a 43 per cent rise in revenue to ₹3,123 crore. EBITDA moved up 30 per cent to ₹616 crore over the same period, suggesting that the topline expansion remained broad-based even as operating pressure became more visible in the quarter. 
 The second quarter alone was even more striking on the revenue line. Consolidated revenue climbed 57.93 per cent year on year to ₹1,691 crore, while EBITDA rose 27.48 per cent to ₹303 crore and profit after tax increased 31.33 per cent to ₹231 crore. On a standalone basis, Q2 revenue stood at ₹1,543 crore, EBITDA at ₹308 crore and profit after tax at ₹240 crore. 
 Yet the numbers also point to a clear trade-off. While sales momentum strengthened, operating efficiency softened sequentially. Management said EBITDA per metric tonne improved to ₹21,000 in the quarter from ₹17,900 a year earlier, but it was lower than the previous quarter’s level, reflecting pressure from freight costs, raw material movements and timing lags in price pass-through. 
 Carbon materials stayed the core engine 
The carbon materials and chemicals business continued to do the heavy lifting, contributing ₹1,539.02 crore to consolidated revenue in the quarter, up from ₹1,067.21 crore in the year-ago period. The power segment also expanded, with revenue rising to ₹33.32 crore from ₹22.90 crore. The “Others” category, which includes mining and related activities, brought in ₹144.14 crore in Q2FY27. 
 Capacity utilisation in the carbon black business was 88 per cent during the quarter. Management indicated a working range of 88 per cent to 95 per cent for the coming period, signalling that the business is still operating with some headroom even as demand stays firm. The company said volume growth accounted for 11 per cent of the topline increase, with the rest supported by higher value realisation and a richer product mix. 
 Battery materials and speciality products move to the forefront 
The bigger story, however, is the strategic shift under way outside traditional carbon black. Himadri is building an integrated platform in advanced materials, with a particular focus on battery-related chemistry and speciality applications. The company has commissioned a 200 MTPA anode material facility at Mahistikry in West Bengal, backed by more than a decade of in-house research and development. The plant has been designed with feedstock flexibility, allowing it to use internally developed materials, and early customer feedback on sample batches has reportedly been positive. 
 Work is also progressing on lithium iron phosphate cathode active materials. A 2,000 MTPA demonstration line is expected to be commissioned in Q3FY27, with a long-term target of 200,000 MTPA. The company has described this as one of the first commercial LFP CAM facilities outside China. In addition, a 40,000 TPA capacity is planned for commissioning next year to support scale-up after customer qualification. 
Another key project is India’s first commercial carbon nanotube plant, with 200 MTPA capacity and a planned commissioning in Q4FY27. The project carries a capex of ₹70 crore. Separately, the company is converting existing carbon black capacity to make super speciality carbon black, adding 6,000 MTPA of high-value output through a ₹170 crore investment, with commissioning targeted for Q4FY28. 
 Investments, overseas push and tyre business add new layers 
Beyond its own plants, the company has been deepening exposure to the battery value chain through investments and partnerships. It owns a 19.44 per cent stake in International Battery Company , which is moving from pre-revenue status towards revenue generation. The India Gigafactory project is expected to be operational in Q1FY28, and the venture is positioned as a technology partner for cell manufacturing rather than a captive consumption play alone. 
The company also has exposure to Sicona Battery Technologies , which recently secured AUD 45 million from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency . Sicona has completed the full acquisition of Advano in the United States, strengthening its silicon anode intellectual property and adding pilot plant capabilities in that market. Another investment, Invati Creations , where the stake stands at 40 per cent, is focused on high-performance electrode materials using nanotech-enabled formulations. 
To widen its international reach, a wholly owned subsidiary, Ardent Impex FZCO , has been incorporated in Dubai Airport Free Zone Area. The entity will handle global sales, marketing and procurement across the Middle East, Africa and Europe. On the downstream side, Birla Tyres , acquired in October 2023, is said to be nearing double-digit market share in select geographies. The brand now operates through 49 distributors, including 40 in India and nine overseas, and more than 1,300 dealers. Management expects entry into the passenger car radial segment by FY28. 
 Balance-sheet strain is visible despite stronger operating scale 
The half-year performance is not without strain. Trade receivables rose to ₹1,026.18 crore as of September 30, 2026, from ₹696.42 crore at the end of March 2026, while current borrowings increased to ₹1,152.26 crore. The company reported negative operating cash flow of ₹91.60 crore for H1FY27, largely because working capital absorbed ₹686.25 crore during the period.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

 Sun Pharma: Nomura retains 'Buy', cuts target price to Rs 2,260 after specialty business slowdown
 The brokerage now values Sun Pharma at 28 times its FY29 estimated earnings per share of Rs 71.9, down from 32.5 times earlier. 
 November 02, 2026 / 13:30 IST 
 Story continues below Advertisement
 Remove Ad 
 Nomura expects specialty growth to improve in FY28 and FY29, supported by Ilumya and new launches. 
 Nomura keeps Buy rating on Sun Pharma, cuts target to Rs 2,260.
 Q2FY27 results beat estimates with strong India market growth.
 Specialty business slowdown led to target price valuation cut.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Nomura has retained its 'Buy' rating on Sun Pharmaceutical Industries but cut its target price to Rs 2,260 from Rs 2,400, citing a slowdown in its specialty business despite strong growth in India. The brokerage expects specialty growth to recover in FY28 and FY29 and remains constructive on the company's proposed acquisition of Organon.
Sun Pharma's Q2FY27 performance came in ahead of Nomura's estimates, with revenue and EBITDA beating its forecasts by 1% and 8%, respectively. Adjusted net profit rose 4% year-on-year to Rs 32.5 billion and was 10% above the brokerage's estimate.
 Growth was in double digits across all key segments except the US, helped partly by favourable currency movements. India revenue increased 17.3% year-on-year, with volume growth of around 6%, compared with 1.6% for the Indian Pharmaceutical Market (IPM).
US sales stood at $455 million, up $28 million sequentially from a seasonally weak base and supported by Levulan and five new generic launches. However, revenue was flat year-on-year as competition in lenalidomide and slower specialty growth offset these gains.
Global innovative medicines, or specialty, sales rose 6.9% year-on-year to $356 million. Management attributed the slowdown to Ilumya in the US. Nomura said interventions are in place and the recently approved indication for psoriatic arthritis should support a gradual recovery.
 Gross margin expanded 147 basis points year-on-year to 80.8%, aided by a richer branded-generic mix and favourable currency movements.
However, EBITDA margin expansion was limited to 43 basis points, taking it to 28.4%, as selling, general and administrative expenses rose due to spending on specialty launches. Research and development expenses stood at 4.8% of sales, below the company's guidance of 6-7%.
 Organon reported revenue of $1.57 billion for the third quarter of calendar year 2026, down 2% year-on-year but up 1% sequentially. Growth in biosimilars, which rose 12%, was partly offset by a 10% decline in women's health, while established brands remained flat.
Nexplanon revenue declined 10% year-on-year due to reinsertion delays and uncertainty around US federal funding. Organon's EBITDA fell 3% year-on-year to $502 million, although it increased 9% sequentially. Management expects the acquisition by Sun Pharma to be completed by the fourth quarter of FY27.
Nomura remains constructive on the transaction and expects Sun Pharma to realise $500 million in synergies, compared with the guided $350 million. Its valuation adds Rs 250 per share for Organon, based on an enterprise value-to-EBITDA multiple of 8 times.
 Target price cut on lower valuation multiple 
Nomura has raised its FY27 EBITDA estimate by around 4%, but cut its net profit estimate by 6% due to an exceptional charge and a higher effective tax rate. Its FY28 and FY29 estimates are broadly unchanged, with a 1% increase.
The brokerage now values Sun Pharma at 28 times its FY29 estimated earnings per share of Rs 71.9, down from 32.5 times earlier. The reduction reflects a higher cost of capital, the valuation roll-forward and multiple compression for domestic formulations amid the specialty business slowdown.
This translates into a value of Rs 2,013 per share for the base business, with an additional Rs 250 per share attributed to Organon, taking the target price to Rs 2,260.
Nomura expects specialty growth to improve in FY28 and FY29, supported by Ilumya and new launches. It also sees strong valuation support from Sun Pharma's domestic formulations and branded-generic businesses. Excluding the Organon valuation, the stock trades at 29 times and 25 times its FY28 and FY29 estimated EPS of Rs 60.9 and Rs 71.9, respectively.

Nomura has retained its 'Buy' rating on United Spirits and raised its target price to Rs 1,700 from Rs 1,600, expecting a stronger performance in the second half of FY27 as the impact of the Maharashtra Mild Liquor (MML) disruption anniversary kicks in and festive demand gathers pace.
The brokerage expects premium and above (P&A) sales growth to return to double digits in the second half of FY27, adding that the anniversary of the MML impact from October could contribute 2-3% to growth. Management has guided for double-digit sales growth in P&A for FY27.
Sales growth remained healthy at 10.5% in the first half of FY27, excluding Maharashtra, including strong performance in Karnataka. The state recorded around 27-30% volume growth and 30-34% value growth in P&A, according to the report.
Nomura expects gross margin (GPM) of 48% to sustain in the second half, supported by a better product mix, including higher growth in Smirnoff, benefits from the India-UK free trade agreement (FTA), and stability or deflation in extra neutral alcohol (ENA) prices during the first and second quarters. While ENA prices have turned inflationary due to El Niño, management expects the full benefits of the India-UK FTA to offset the impact.
The West Asia crisis increased costs by around Rs 500 million in the second quarter across glass, energy, packaging and logistics. Operating margin stood at 19.7% in Q2FY27, supported by lower employee and other expenses following organisational simplification.
Advertising and promotion (A&P) spending rose 57% year-on-year in the second quarter and is expected to remain elevated. Management said the spending was consciously front-loaded ahead of the festive season to improve product availability, brand recall and consumption. The FY27 A&P guidance for the core portfolio remains around 11% of net sales, with additional investment planned for new launches such as Smirnoff Ice.
Smirnoff continues to grow strongly and is on track to achieve its net sales value aspiration of more than Rs 10 billion in FY27. United Spirits has introduced two new flavours, Kaccha Mango and Coffee Toffee.
The company has launched Smirnoff Ice in the ready-to-drink segment, with variants at 4.8% and 8% alcohol by volume (ABV) in Goa and Mumbai. Bengaluru is next in line. The launch is expected to expand consumption occasions and attract consumers from beer and wine. The report notes that the product has a three-times multiplier to the core brand as drinkers graduate.
 United Spirits has also relaunched J&B whisky as a 100% Scotch at a competitive price point, enabled by the India-UK FTA. The brand, which has 60% national salience, is aimed at recruiting new consumers and deepening Scotch penetration ahead of the festive season. As a Diageo global trademark, it falls within the 10% margin cap.
The McDowell 's relaunch has received a mixed response, with 80-85% of markets covered. The response has been positive in West Bengal, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana, where United Spirits is not the market leader. However, some conservative leader markets resisted the new PET packaging, prompting a return to glass packaging.
On the Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) transaction, management expects the deal to close by mid-December. Competition Commission of India approval has been received, while the BCCI's due diligence is at an advanced stage.
Nomura has marginally tweaked its earnings estimates and forecasts a 16% compound annual growth rate in earnings per share over FY27-29. It values United Spirits using a sum-of-the-parts approach, with the valuation rolled forward to December 2028 from June 2028 earlier, as the RCB sale is yet to conclude. The revised target price is Rs 1,700. United Spirits trades at 44 times its March 2028 estimated EPS.
The key risk to Nomura's view is slower growth in the P&A segment.

Reliance Industries Ltd shares have secured bullish ratings following the company’s record September quarter earnings. Goldman Sachs and Nomura have maintained their Buy ratings on the stock, citing strong performance in its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business and steady growth in telecom, even as retail earnings remained under pressure.
Goldman Sachs set a target price of Rs 1,840 per share, implying 58 percent upside from Friday's closing price, while Nomura assigned a target of Rs 1,560 per share.
 Reliance Industries shares closed at Rs 1,164.90 on Friday, October 30, down 0.21 percent ahead of the company's Q2 FY27 results announcement. The Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate had a market capitalisation of Rs 15.76 lakh crore.
Reliance Industries reported its strongest-ever quarterly financial performance in the fiscal second quarter, with record revenue, EBITDA and net profit, driven by robust growth in its O2C business, digital services and retail operations.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
Consolidated revenue surged 28 percent year-on-year to an all-time high of Rs 3.62 lakh crore, while EBITDA increased 24 percent to a record Rs 62,409 crore. Net profit jumped 34 percent to Rs 29,550 crore, also a quarterly record.
The O2C business delivered its strongest-ever quarterly performance, with revenue rising 44.2 percent year-on-year to Rs 2.32 lakh crore and EBITDA surging 67.9 percent to Rs 25,203 crore.
According to Goldman Sachs, Reliance's Q2 EBITDA beat its estimates by 9 percent, led by strong O2C performance. However, Goldman Sachs expects refining margins to moderate in the third quarter due to higher very large crude carrier (VLCC) freight costs, although this could be partly offset by processing discounted heavy crude.
The brokerage said that Reliance Retail's EBITDA declined 11 percent year-on-year, while revenue growth slowed to 6.4 percent from 11 percent in the preceding quarter, reflecting the timing of festive demand and investments in JioMart. Retail EBITDA margin contracted 140 basis points year-on-year.
On Reliance's new energy business, Goldman Sachs said the company's solar module and cell manufacturing capacities of 6 GW and 5 GW, respectively, remain on track to reach 20 GW each in the first half of next year. Battery pack and container facilities are expected to ramp up in the first half of calendar year 2027, followed by battery cell facilities in the second half.
The Kutch-Jamnagar renewable energy power transmission project is targeted for completion in the first quarter of 2027, while earnings contributions from renewable energy and round-the-clock power operations are expected from FY28.
Nomura attributed Reliance's record second-quarter performance to multi-decade-high refining cracks, adding that consolidated EBITDA rose 19 percent sequentially and exceeded its estimates by 9 percent, driven primarily by the O2C segment.
Nomura said the telecom business continued to deliver steady growth, while retail performance remained soft due to the shift in festive demand and ongoing investments in digital commerce. The brokerage said that Reliance Industries trades at 8.7 times its estimated FY28 enterprise value-to-EBITDA ratio and 16.5 times its estimated FY28 price-to-earnings ratio.

 Ambuja Cements shares gain nearly 4% on new investment worth Rs 14,500 crore; Nomura retains ‘Buy’ but cuts target price
 Nomura expects RM+PF costs per tonne to increase 5% sequentially in Q3FY27, limiting the improvement in EBITDA per tonne to around Rs 75 sequentially, to Rs 845.

 November 02, 2026 / 12:08 IST 
 --> 
 The brokerage's revised target price of Rs 470 implies an upside of 32.4% from the October 29 closing price of Rs 355. 
 Ambuja Cements plans Rs 14,500 crore capex for expansion.
 Nomura maintains Buy on Ambuja, cuts target price to Rs 470.
 Q2 EBITDA beat driven by better-than-expected realisations.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Ambuja Cements share were seen trading green on Monday November 2 after the company announced that it is preparing for its next phase of growth with a total capex of around Rs 14,500 crore.
The new expansion is expected to add 30 metric tonne per annum of cement across key markets.
The company’s stocks were trading at Rs 360.95 on the NSE, up Rs 12.90 or 3.71% at 11:52 am.
Nomura has maintained its 'Buy' rating on Ambuja Cements but cut its target price by 6% to Rs 470 from Rs 500, citing operational challenges, cost pressures and concerns over the company's accelerated capacity expansion plans.
The brokerage said its earlier constructive view was based on management's shift towards asset sweating rather than capacity-led growth. However, the announced addition of around 30 million tonnes of cement capacity and 10 million tonnes of clinker capacity, at an investment of Rs 14,500 crore, partially departs from that strategy.
Nomura noted that the acquired assets are operating at around 50% utilisation, below Ambuja's own levels in the same regions, while the company's EBITDA per tonne continues to trail peers. "Against this backdrop, accelerating capacity additions appears premature," it said.
The brokerage pointed out that 51% of the proposed new cement capacity is in the West, Ambuja's stronghold, where ramp-up should be smoother. However, the East and Northeast, which account for 39% of the new capacity, are characterised by intense competition and entrenched incumbents, potentially delaying utilisation and returns.
While Nomura raised its volume estimates, it lowered its EBITDA per tonne estimates for FY27, FY28 and FY29 by 11%, 5% and 7%, respectively, citing weaker fixed-cost absorption and external cost pressures. It has also reduced its one-year forward target multiple to 13x from 15x and rolled forward its valuation to December 2028.
 Better realisations support Q2 EBITDA beat 
Ambuja Cements reported Q2FY27 EBITDA of Rs 1,270 crore, 7% above Nomura's forecast, although 1% below the Bloomberg consensus estimate. The outperformance was largely driven by better-than-expected realisations.
Volumes stood at 16.5 million tonnes, down 1% year-on-year and 3% below the brokerage's estimates, partly due to plant shutdowns. Operating costs per tonne increased 4% sequentially, driven by elevated fuel and logistics costs, and were 1% above Nomura's estimate.
Consequently, EBITDA per tonne came in at Rs 770, down around Rs 160 sequentially but 11% above the brokerage's forecast.
 Cost pressures to limit margin recovery in Q3 
For Q3FY27, Nomura expects blended realisations to improve 2% sequentially as cement prices recover after seasonal weakness. It also expects cementitious volumes to grow 9% year-on-year.
However, fuel costs remain a concern. Management indicated spot blended fuel costs of Rs 2.85 per kcal for the group, compared with the Q2FY27 average of Rs 1.87 per kcal. This is likely to keep raw material and power and fuel (RM+PF) costs per tonne elevated in the December quarter.
Nomura expects RM+PF costs per tonne to increase 5% sequentially in Q3FY27, limiting the improvement in EBITDA per tonne to around Rs 75 sequentially, to Rs 845.
The brokerage's revised target price of Rs 470 implies an upside of 32.4% from the October 29 closing price of Rs 355.

docs.text:
News 
 Cybercrime surge drives rush for white-collar crime lawyers
 Krishna Yadav , Yash Tiwari 5 min read 2 Nov 2026, 06:00 AM IST 
 Summary
 Their work is also shifting from routine compliance audits to risk assessment, incident response and investigations, they said. White-collar crimes are typically committed by entities 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Cyber fraud is becoming a bigger and more complex threat for India Inc., with criminals impersonating company bosses, siphoning off funds and stealing customer data, sometimes through vulnerable vendors. Now, with artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled scams adding to the risks, white-collar crime teams at law firms are seeing a 20-30% rise in cybersecurity-related advisory and investigation work, lawyers said. 
 Their work is also shifting from routine compliance audits to risk assessment, incident response and investigations, they said. White-collar crimes are typically committed by entities. 
 “We have seen a significant increase, perhaps 20-30% more than previous years, in advisory work relating to criminal investigations being conducted by law enforcement agencies into various cybercrimes against or involving technology and banking companies,” said Dheeraj Nair, partner at JSA Advocates & Solicitors. 
 Nair said JSA was advising clients on frozen bank accounts in cyberfraud cases, customer-data theft, police requests for overseas-held data, regulatory reporting and data breach disputes. Companies were also seeking proactive data protection advice. 
 Shahana Chatterji, partner at Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co., attributed the development to higher regulatory scrutiny. “We have seen a tangible increase in client questions around cybersecurity incidents, specifically on how to effectively manage and mitigate them. This is largely driven by heightened regulatory scrutiny and upcoming obligations under new privacy laws,” said. 
 India’s Digital Personal Data Protection ( DPDP ) Act, 2023, and DPDP Rules, 2025, set out requirements for consent, data security, breach reporting and individuals’ privacy rights. With most substantive obligations taking effect on 13 May 2027, companies are reviewing data practices, vendor arrangements and breach-response plans to prepare for compliance.
 Supratim Chakraborty, partner at Khaitan & Co., said mandates now covered the entire incident lifecycle, from pre-incident preparedness and legal assistance during attacks to regulatory notifications, communication with affected individuals and post-incident remediation. 
 The growing legal workload comes as companies ramp up cybersecurity spending. US technology research firm Gartner projected India's information-security spending at $3.4 billion in 2026, up 11.7% from 2025. A Tata Tele Business Services-CMR survey of 800 small and medium enterprise IT heads across eight cities found that 84% planned to increase cybersecurity budgets over the following 12-24 months. 
 Narasimhan Elangovan, co-founder and cyber security and data privacy practice leader at Ascentium India, said companies were investing in cybersecurity tools and talent to protect assets and build customer trust, with attacks often prompting further spending. 
 “After an attack, organizations learn a lot through forensics. This leads to incremental investments... Often, incidents are also wake-up calls for many organizations,” he said. Elangovan said companies seek advice on incident response, regulatory reporting, vendor breaches, cyber insurance, compliance of The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act), and risks associated with employees using public AI tools. 
 The changing nature of cyber fraud is reflected in cases law firms are handling. 
 Kunal Gupta, partner in Trilegal's white-collar crime practice, said fraudsters were using publicly available information, including LinkedIn profiles and regulatory filings, to map corporate hierarchies and impersonate executives through spoofed WhatsApp profiles and emails.
 In one case, funds were misappropriated using a spoofed executive identity created through a publicly available domain service. “Such frauds do not always involve technically sophisticated methods. A failure to notice anomalies in an email address or question an unusual payment request can allow relatively simple frauds to succeed,” Gupta said. 
 JSA has handled cases involving theft of customer information, including credit card and know-your-customer data, through vendors and sub-vendors such as call centres working for banks. “Breaches are taking place not within the client directly, but with a vendor or sub-vendor, who is a weak link,” Nair said. The firm has also seen fraudsters exploit e-commerce software glitches to obtain both products and refunds, or manipulate electronic gift vouchers. 
 Khaitan has flagged AI -enabled threats such as phishing, deepfake impersonation of executives and fraudulent payment authorizations. Companies are also concerned about employees inadvertently disclosing confidential information through generative AI tools.
 Frauds of all shades 
 Recent incidents underline these risks. 
 On 21 October, the country's largest lender State Bank of India disclosed a suspected data leak after identifying 3,897 customer records with personal identifiable information among approximately 3.75 lakh records examined on the dark web.
 Two Mumbai-based non-bank lenders reportedly lost around $2 million in more than 700 unauthorized transfers on 8-9 October, according to a Reuters report of 30 October. Hackers allegedly compromised the application programming interface (API) used to send loan-disbursement instructions to ICICI Bank. 
 Tata Electronics had also confirmed a cybersecurity incident in June after a ransomware group claimed to have leaked company data, including documents purportedly linked to Apple and Tesla.

docs.title: Why investors may be ready to return to large-cap stocks
docs.text:
Mint Money 
 Why investors may be ready to return to large-cap stocks
 Shyam Sekhar 4 min read 2 Nov 2026, 12:52 PM IST 
 Summary
 After years of money chasing small- and mid-cap funds, stretched valuations and weakening earnings are prompting investors to reconsider large-cap stocks. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Mutual fund investing has rarely followed a more inverted pattern than it does today. Capital has persistently chased small-cap and mid-cap funds, with money flowing largely one way into these categories through lump-sum investments. Investors have shunned bluechip-heavy large-cap funds, while incremental growth in the SIP book has also come largely from small-cap and mid-cap categories. The prevailing belief was that large-caps could no longer deliver the growth potential of these emerging categories.
 Strong inflows certainly helped small- and mid-cap stocks show strength and resilience for several quarters. However, two factors have changed the picture in recent months: a sharp spike in commodity prices and the significant valuation premium at which these market favourites trade relative to the rest of the market.
 Discerning investors have begun trimming positions in overvalued stocks, while selling pressure is rising rapidly in companies that show even the slightest disappointment in quarterly results. Investors are also factoring in the impact of sustained commodity inflation on future demand, sales growth and margins.
 At the same time, the sharp contraction in large-cap valuations has significantly widened the gap between these companies and the market's favourites. This has made investors more conscious of the relative attractiveness of large-caps, given their discount to historical valuations, strong ability to revive growth and superior balance sheets. These companies also have the capacity to reduce their capital base through share buybacks.
 The prospect of management teams initiating buybacks, even amid investor apathy, is real. We are also seeing preferential issues in which promoters are buying shares in bluechips. Bajaj Finance is a prime example. In much-hated sectors such as life insurance, promoters are raising their stakes at historically low valuations; ICICI Life is one example.
 There are several signs of management teams and boards stepping in to signal confidence in companies even as the market overlooks their merits. Yet, this confidence is still not translating into broader investor interest. The bias against large-cap investing remains strong, with investor aversion at a historic high.
 Early signs of rotation 
 But the tide could be turning, although it may still be too early to call. For starters, the sharp correction in September and October has reopened the debate over whether blindly buying small-cap funds at any valuation can continue to work.
 The lack of growth in the large-cap space, coupled with relentless selling by foreign institutional investors ( FIIs ), continues to keep the broader segment weak, weighing on performance and sentiment. Meanwhile, mid-cap and small-cap fund performance has also begun to weaken this results season.
 Companies held by these funds are being punished when they fail to meet stretched investor expectations. Stocks are seeing sell-offs even when quarterly performance is reasonable. Those reporting earnings disappointments are suffering sharper drawdowns as investors rapidly unwind positions they once held with conviction.
 This erosion of investor conviction is sending a broader warning to those bidding up IPO prices on listing and buying into companies reporting strong quarterly results during a favourable earnings cycle.
 At the same time, falling valuations in already cheap companies are creating contrarian buying opportunities in several bluechips, although the buying remains sporadic and selective. The recent rally in IT stocks is a good example of how confidence can return to a sector that was widely disliked and had seen a sharp correction.
 The growth question 
 The road to recovery, however, will be slow and painful, and investors will have to climb over a wall of fear. Still, the market mood suggests that fatigue with expensive segments such as small-caps and mid-caps could trigger a rotation towards attractively valued large-cap companies.
 The sharp rebound in bluechip IT stocks could spread to other beaten-down sectors where valuations have become difficult to ignore. The main factor holding back this rotation is uncertainty over when growth will return in sectors such as consumption and pharmaceuticals, or when net interest margins and return on assets will expand in banking and financial services.
 As visibility improves, more factors providing directional confidence will emerge. As investors grow more sceptical of overvalued companies, opportunistic capital could begin moving towards businesses where value is more evident. Even small positive developments would start attracting greater investor attention, while relatively minor negatives may be overlooked.
 Investors would gradually begin bargain-hunting for value in bluechips. Slowly, the wheels of the market would start turning.
 For now, investors have only begun rethinking their aggressive investment stance, prompted by weakness in overvalued stocks. The remainder of the results season could accelerate this reassessment. Mutual fund investors may need to review their portfolios and reposition them before the tide turns decisively.
 Shyam Sekhar is chief ideator and founder of ithought Financial Consulting LLP.

docs.title: Got a Diwali gift from your employer? Check the tax rules
docs.text:
Mint Money Got a Diwali gift from your employer? Check the tax rules Aprajita Sharma 4 min read 2 Nov 2026, 01:14 PM IST Summary Employer gifts worth less than ₹ 15,000 may be tax-free, but bonuses are taxable from the first rupee. Here's how the rules work and when a bonus can increase your tax bill. Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now Awaiting your Diwali gift from your employer, or have you already received one? Before celebrating, make sure you understand the tax implications. While gifts from employers can be tax-free up to a specified limit, bonuses are taxable from the very first rupee. The distinction could make a significant difference to your tax liability. The Income-tax Act, 2025, which came into effect on 1 April 2026 and replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961, has raised the annual tax-exempt limit for gifts received from employers to less than ₹ 15,000, from less than ₹ 5,000 earlier. "The exemption applies from tax year 2026-27 (FY27). The gift exemption limit of ₹ 15,000 covers non-cash gifts, vouchers and tokens, including physical gifts and digital gift cards redeemable for goods or services, provided their aggregate value is below ₹ 15,000 during the tax year. Gifts to a member of the employee's household are also covered," said SR Patnaik, Partner (head-taxation), Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas. If the total value of gifts reaches ₹ 15,000 or exceeds it, the entire amount becomes taxable. "Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 states that when the aggregate value of all gifts in a tax year is less than ₹ 15,000, only then the value of such gifts shall be considered as 'nil'. Hence, conservatively, the entire aggregate value of all gifts may become taxable as a part of salary in the hands of the employees," Patnaik said. For instance, if your employer gives you a mobile phone worth ₹ 10,000 during Diwali and you receive another gift worth ₹ 4,000 later in the same tax year, the aggregate value of ₹ 14,000 remains tax-free. But if the total value reaches or crosses ₹ 15,000, the entire amount becomes taxable. Gift or bonus? Not every payment received during Diwali qualifies as a gift. Cash payments, including Diwali bonuses, are generally treated as salary and taxed accordingly. "Even cash gifts will fall under this limit as long as the same is gratuitous from employer. If it comes as Diwali or professional bonus, it will not fall under the ₹ 15,000 limit and will be 100% taxable as salary from the first rupee," Patnaik said. The tax treatment also determines whether the employer needs to deduct tax at source (TDS). Employers do not have to deduct TDS if the aggregate value of gifts is below ₹ 15,000. TDS is required when the value exceeds ₹ 15,000. "Gifts more than ₹ 15,000 would be taxable in the hands of the employee and would be considered as part of their salary when received from the employer whether in kind or in cash. The employer is required to deduct TDS on such gifts which is usually adjusted from the regular monthly salary of the employee. The employee can verify that the gift amount has been considered in his income in Form 130 (previously Form 16) and the employer has deducted tax accordingly on it," said Ankit Jain, Partner, Ved Jain and Associates. Form 16 has been replaced and renumbered as Form 130 from 1 April 2026, for tax year 2026-27 onwards. The rebate trap While employees receiving non-cash gifts within the exemption limit need not worry about an additional tax liability , those receiving cash bonuses should assess how the payment affects their overall taxable income. This is particularly relevant for salaried individuals earning close to ₹ 12.75 lakh annually under the new tax regime. Under Section 87A, resident individual taxpayers with taxable income of up to ₹ 12 lakh can claim a rebate, effectively bringing their tax liability to nil. For salaried employees, the ₹ 75,000 standard deduction takes the corresponding gross salary threshold to ₹ 12.75 lakh, assuming they have no other income. Consider an employee earning an annual salary of ₹ 12.60 lakh. After the standard deduction of ₹ 75,000, the taxable income works out to ₹ 11.85 lakh, keeping it within the ₹ 12 lakh rebate limit. Now, if the employee receives a Diwali bonus of ₹ 50,000, gross salary rises to ₹ 13.10 lakh and taxable income to ₹ 12.35 lakh. The employee will no longer qualify for the full Section 87A rebate and will have a tax liability. Including health and education cess, the tax would amount to ₹ 36,400. This effectively reduces the bonus of ₹ 50,000 to ₹ 13,600 after tax. Therefore, while a Diwali bonus may appear to offer an additional financial cushion, employees earning close to the tax-free income threshold should account for the additional tax it could trigger. Unlike an eligible gift, a bonus can push their income beyond the rebate threshold and increase their tax outgo. docs.title: How to enjoy Diwali without giving your savings a hangover
docs.text:
Mint Money 
 How to enjoy Diwali without giving your savings a hangover
 Ananya Grover 7 min read 2 Nov 2026, 12:25 PM IST 
 Summary
 Layoff fears, muted salary hikes and rising prices are making households more cautious this festive season. Experts say plan your splurges without depleting savings or taking on debt. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 The festive season traditionally brings the highest consumer spending among Indian households. A recent report by YouGov and Rukam Capital found that 60% of Gen Z shoppers increase their spending during major festivals, with 25% spending significantly more and 35% somewhat more.
 But the world around us is changing. News of layoffs in the IT sector, muted salary hikes and inflation inching up again warrant a closer look at how households spend and splurge. We spoke to individuals to gauge the mood and to experts on how households should respond.
 Why people splurge 
 Diwali is usually when families want to celebrate, buy something new and gift friends and relatives. The festive spirit makes spending part of the occasion. Preeti Zende, a Sebi-registered investment adviser and founder of Apanadhan Financial Services, said people also tend to spend impulsively because of the fear of missing out ( FOMO ) fuelled by social media influencers.
 Many people also have extra money in hand through bonuses or variable pay, which can tempt them to treat it as “free money” for celebrations, said Arindam Banerjee, professor and programme director of the Masters of Applied Finance & Wealth Management at SP Jain School of Global Management.
 The market is designed to reinforce this mood. Retailers, banks and digital platforms all target consumers with offers during this period, lowering their resistance to spending. “Cashback, no-cost EMIs, limited-time deals and social pressure all arrive together,” Banerjee said. In a normal year, he added, this may be manageable for a household with a stable income. But this year, households may need to tread more carefully.
 What’s different this time 
 In fact, many households have already begun exercising financial prudence. According to Sachin Taparia, founder and CEO of LocalCircles, urban households are likely to spend an average of ₹ 20,000 this festive season, down from around ₹ 45,000 last year. They are scaling back mainly on big-ticket purchases, with no tax tailwind comparable to last year's GST cuts and credit becoming costlier after the RBI's 7 October rate hike.
 In its latest survey, LocalCircles found that 31% of the 22,904 respondents had no discretionary spending planned this festive season . “People are not making big-ticket purchases as phones and appliances have become costlier, anxiety about white-collar job security is making employees hold back and small business owners are also facing competition from quick commerce giants,” Taparia said.
 The steady stream of layoff announcements in the IT sector is adding to the uncertainty. US-based AI firm Innodata abruptly fired nearly 550 Indian employees on Monday, while Microsoft extended a massive global Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to its 23,000-strong Indian workforce, with a 1 December deadline. Oracle has downsized about 10% of its local team, or roughly 3,000 employees, in its latest engineering-heavy job cuts. Reports indicate that IT may extend a Voluntary Separation Programme (VSP) to remaining Indian managerial roles as it builds out massive AI data centre infrastructure.
 Banerjee explained that when an IT professional loses a job, the financial shock extends well beyond the individual. Many households have a home loan, a car EMI, school fees and often parents in another city to support. A mid-level professional who loses a job may also take longer to find an equivalent role than during previous downturns. Households should therefore plan for a longer period without income rather than assume a quick recovery, he said.
 That is exactly what Savrat Vaish, a Delhi-based sales manager, is planning to do. He intends to put most of his Diwali bonus into savings and is also cutting down on midnight food orders and designer clothes. “I want to enjoy Diwali, but also maintain financial discipline amid the uncertainty,” he said.
 Saurabh Singh, an assistant finance manager, is also cutting out unnecessary expenses. He plans to avoid excess spending because he has several expenses lined up for which he has been saving through mutual funds from an early age. Even while redeeming his mutual funds, he has decided to not use the entire funds but deploy a portion of it along with his Diwali bonus back into investments when the timing is right.
 Spend without the hangover 
 Even as LocalCircles' survey points to lower spending this season, a large section of households will still fund festive purchases, to varying degrees, from their savings. In the survey, 83% of the 23,451 respondents said they planned to dip into savings to some extent, while 16% said they would rely entirely on savings to fund their spending. That is a worrying sign.
 For those considering dipping into savings, Taparia poses an important question: “How many more festivals can you celebrate from savings unless your earnings increase?”
 Using savings to fund festivities can leave household finances nursing a hangover long after the celebrations are over. According to Banerjee, savings act as insurance against income loss. Using them for discretionary purchases now means entering what could be a difficult few months with a thinner financial cushion. “If celebrations must be funded, use the monthly surplus and leave the reserve alone,” he said.
 But households should be careful not only about dipping into savings. Purchases financed through credit offers such as no-cost EMIs also need scrutiny. EMIs and festive financing can make a ₹ 1.2 lakh television feel like a ₹ 10,000-a-month decision.
