Global 
 Trump surprises Republicans with election eve speech about reflecting pool
 Alex Leary , Marianne LeVine , Philip Wegmann , The Wall Street Journal 5 min read 3 Nov 2026, 06:29 AM IST 
 Summary
 The president delivered remarks in front of the Lincoln Memorial on Monday that focused on his construction projects. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 WASHINGTON—It was a picture-perfect setting for the closing argument of a contentious campaign season. But when President Trump stepped up to a lectern in front of the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool on Monday afternoon, he had another matter on his mind: rusty pipes.
 “The pipes were very old and in bad shape,” Trump said, holding up photos of the aging infrastructure he replaced under the reflecting pool. “The pipes now are totally renovated. They’re brand new pipes.”
 The president’s nearly hourlong speech, which some White House officials pitched as a capstone to a flurry of midterm election rallies, centered on the many construction projects and renovations Trump has overseen during his second term. He talked about cleaning up graffiti, fixing fountains and monuments, and resodding the National Mall.
 “Like the human being, grass has a life also,” Trump said. “The grass in front of the White House was a very inferior grass for many, many years, and now it’s beautiful.”
 The remarks frustrated Republicans, including some of his own White House advisers, who privately expressed exasperation that the president chose not to use a high-profile speech on the eve of the election to squarely focus on the economic issues that voters say they care most about. In recent days, GOP operatives have grown increasingly worried that they will suffer far-reaching losses in this week’s election—and the mood inside the White House has grown dour.
 Asked for a response to the speech, a person close to the president texted a facepalm emoji. A prominent Republican strategist said the backdrop was great, but the message was wrong. Another Republican operative said that the algae that has plagued the reflecting pool would be the least of their problems if Republicans lose the House and Senate on Tuesday.
 “He has never been known for message discipline,” said retiring Nebraska Republican Rep. Don Bacon. He had hoped that Trump would focus more on GOP accomplishments such as tax cuts and border security, topics that the president touched on in passing during his speech. Bacon added that it wasn’t all bad: “At least he wasn’t talking about men’s behinds.”
 After the speech, some Trump advisers argued that the remarks weren’t intended to be a closing message. But a senior White House official previewed the speech to reporters in exactly those terms on Sunday, saying the remarks would serve as a final argument to voters and an opportunity for the president to tout Republican accomplishments.
 Trump views beautification of Washington as one of his strongest legacies, and he has told advisers it inspires pride in the country. Aides have privately encouraged him to focus on other things, but the president has largely rejected that advice, believing that the issue will resonate with voters. Polls have shown that a majority of Americans disapprove of his construction projects, including the new White House ballroom, though most Republicans view them positively.
 “The president’s a builder. You can’t keep him away,” Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said Monday at the event.
 Trump had been expected to spend Monday speaking at two or more rallies across the country, part of a monthlong effort to motivate his conservative base to show up at the polls. But he decided instead to dial into a series of virtual rallies and give remarks at the Lincoln Memorial, something he had been angling to do for weeks, according to people familiar with the matter.
 “We’re giving serious thought to changing the name to the Trump Reflecting Pool,” the president said at the beginning of his remarks, clarifying that he was joking.
 The scene was the latest episode in an election filled with unusual moments. Trump, wearing a white USA ball cap, delivered a 53-minute meandering speech to an audience that consisted of a small group of National Park Service workers and members of the media.
 Trump stood next to a large photo of the reflecting pool with the caption: “Back, and more beautiful than ever!” He delivered some of the same lines featured in rally speeches, but without the raucous applause that typically accompanies them. Instead, the scene was mostly quiet—the reflecting pool’s adjacent sidewalks were shut down as a security precaution.
 He spent a small portion of his speech on the election, attacking Democratic candidates as radicals and touting the tax cuts he signed into law.
 Trump earlier this year ordered up a renovation of the historic pool, saying he would do it quicker and cheaper than others. But plans to open it in time for America’s 250th birthday celebration were derailed when green algae blooms appeared.
 Trump also accused vandals of slashing the new liner—which he painted “American flag blue”—though charges were dropped and the contractor acknowledged it had made mistakes.
 As the president touted the new coating he had installed on the bottom of the reflecting pool, he asked, “Does somebody have those pictures for me?” An aide came to the lectern with a stack of photos and Trump offered commentary as he held them up. “These are the pipes,” he said, adding, “That’s brand new grass that was vandalized.”
 Trump views the renovation as part of a larger project to restore the standing of the U.S.
 “We were laughed at all over the world for four years,” he concluded. “We were laughed at like we were stupid people. We were laughed at by every ruler, every president, every prime minister, every king, every queen. But they don’t laugh anymore.”
 Write to Alex Leary at alex

 Japanese investors deepen India bets, creating a bigger business opportunity for law firms
 Sneha Shah , Devina Sengupta 4 min read 2 Nov 2026, 05:59 AM IST 
 Summary
 Sifting sands of geopolitics has meant that India and Japan come closer. Last year, Japan pledged a target of JPY 10 trillion in private and public investments into India over the next decade. Since Aug 2025, 120 MoUs have been signed targeting over ₹ 1 trillion of cross border investments 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 MUMBAI: Japanese money is flowing into India, and the lawyers who handle M&A, PE and venture deals are feeling the surge. Japan desks at leading Indian law firms report their busiest stretch in recent memory, with some adding lawyers and others racing to capture a bigger share of a growing fee pool.
 The momentum shows in a run of investments and partnerships announced over the past 12-18 months. MUFG Bank acquired a 20% stake in Shriram Finance, launched a dedicated venture capital fund for Indian start-ups and signed a strategic partnership with State Bank of India. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation took a 20% stake in YES Bank, and Mizuho Securities plans to acquire a controlling stake in Avendus Capital. The Development Bank of Japan invested in HDFC Capital’s H-DREAM Fund.
 "Due to the increasing deal flow between India and Japan, across M&A and venture and PE investments, our lawyers covering the India-Japan corridor are finding themselves the busiest in the last 12-18 months,'' said Abhishek Guha, partner, corporate practice, at Trilegal. ``We are eyeing an increased volume of M&A and PE-related activity in this corridor going forward and are gearing up for a busy time ahead."
 The growing engagement comes amid shifting global geopolitics, the Russia-Ukraine war and rising US tariffs, which have brought India and Japan closer. Japan was among India's largest sources of foreign direct investment (FDI) equity inflows in the first half of 2026, investing $6.26 billion during January-June, according to government data.
"The India-Japan investment corridor is witnessing remarkable momentum, driven by global economic realignment, changing supply-chain strategies and India's strong growth prospects," said Rudra Kumar Pandey, partner and head of Japan desk at Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co.
 Last year, Japan pledged 10 trillion yen (around $65-100 billion) in public and private investments in India over the next decade. Since August 2025, 120 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) targeting more than ₹ 1 lakh crore in cross-border investments have been signed, government data shows.
 India attractive destination 
 With Japanese companies reassessing their exposure to China amid rising competitive and profitability pressures, India is emerging as an attractive destination for long-term expansion. Against projected global growth of approximately 3.1%, emerging-market growth of around 3.7% and relatively modest growth across major advanced economies, India's growth trajectory stands out, Pandey said.
 India's expanding network of free trade agreements also offers Japanese businesses opportunities to collaborate with Indian companies, establish manufacturing operations and use the country as an export hub.
 "We are witnessing growing interest from Japanese corporations, financial institutions, private capital investors and, increasingly, small and medium enterprises. I expect this diversification to sustain strong momentum in cross-border M&A, joint ventures and investment activity over the coming decade," Pandey added.
 Japanese venture capital (VC) firms and institutional investors are also increasingly shifting their focus from Southeast Asia to India, drawn by stronger IPO momentum, rising exit opportunities and a more vibrant technology start-up ecosystem, Mint reported earlier.
 BeyondNext Ventures, Enrission India Capital, Incubate Fund Asia and Genesia Ventures are among the Japanese VC firms exploring India more aggressively as investments in their home market and Southeast Asia have failed to deliver significant exits.
 More business 
 The growing activity has translated into more business for law firms advising Japanese clients. Firms are responding by forging partnerships with Japanese law firms and hiring lawyers to handle the potential increase in work.
 In September, Argus Partners hired an entire team led by Saurav Kumar from CMS IndusLaw. Kumar joined as senior partner in the firm's corporate and M&A practice and head of its Japan and South Korea desk.
 "The nature of engagements in this corridor has broadened considerably, with significant deal activity emerging in green investments, critical manufacturing and new-age technology sectors. As transactions in these specialized domains were historically uncommon in the Indian market, they introduce intricate regulatory, legal and operational complexities that demand an exceptionally high calibre of legal expertise," said Kumar.
 On the private capital side, the pace of activity has also picked up. Around half a dozen deals and investment announcements have emerged over the past 12-18 months, including the transactions and partnerships involving MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho and DBJ.
 "These are not small stakes or small deals. They are large, complex acquisitions involving significant investments by Japanese financial institutions. This reflects growing confidence in their understanding of India's legal and regulatory environment, and a deep conviction in the country's growth story," said Rishabh Shroff, partner, co-head of private client and head of international business development at Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas.

 Mankind Pharma delivered a strong Q2FY27 performance, supported by healthy growth across domestic formulations, BSV and international markets. Mankind posted 17 per cent Y-o-Y sales growth in Q2FY27, while Ebitda grew faster at 27 per cent Y-o-Y, resulting in 210 bps Y-o-Y margin expansion to 27 per cent, driven by gross margin gains and operating leverage. As per IQVIA, Mankind delivered 15.7 per cent Y-o-Y growth in secondary prescription sales in Q2FY27, 100 bps ahead of the IPM. More importantly, the volume growth trajectory continued to strengthen, rising to 6.7 per cent Y-o-Y from 4.7 per cent in Q1FY27 and 0.5 per cent/2.3 per cent in FY25/FY26. BSV sustained its +20 per cent Y-o-Y growth trajectory, supported by robust performance across domestic and international markets. Management expects international sales to maintain double-digit growth in FY27, driven by new US launches and deeper penetration of BSV’s branded specialty portfolio in emerging markets.
 Mankind has highlighted eight pillars to drive the next leg of growth. The company aims to increase its chronic mix to 50 per cent by FY30E from ~39 per cent currently, supported by new specialty divisions and field-force expansion, while scaling the hospital business to ~5 per cent of sales from ~1.7 per cent and targeting a Top 3 position across 10 focus states. The company aims to create more megabrands from its existing portfolio and broaden its OTC presence beyond sexual wellness into wider wellness segments and new-age channels. Alongside, BSV provides a scalable platform in high-barrier specialty and biologics segments, supported by deeper market penetration and geographic expansion. Mankind remains focused on disciplined capital allocation, prioritizing debt reduction, growth capex, R&D/in-licensing and acquisitions of innovative assets such as ACTx.
 After a prolonged restructuring impact, Mankind’s base business is showing tangible signs of recovery, reflected in improving volume growth, a richer chronic-care product mix and sustained momentum in BSV.  Dr Lal PathLabs is one of India's leading diagnostic service providers, with a strong presence across pathology, wellness and preventive healthcare testing. The company operates an extensive hub-and-spoke network comprising reference laboratories, patient service centres and collection points across the country, enabling it to serve a large and growing customer base. Its business is predominantly B2C focused, supported by a trusted brand, strong quality standards and a growing portfolio of specialized and preventive healthcare offerings. Over the years, DLPL has strengthened its presence beyond its traditional North India markets through network expansion and acquisitions, while also exploring selective international opportunities.
 We remain positive on DLPL given its strong positioning in a structurally attractive diagnostics industry. Rising health awareness, increasing incidence of lifestyle diseases and the ongoing shift from unorganized to organized diagnostic players continue to drive industry growth. DLPL is well placed to capture this opportunity through its strong brand equity, extensive network, high service quality and leadership in preventive healthcare diagnostics. The company is also benefiting from calibrated expansion into underserved markets, including rural areas, where its outreach initiatives are helping deepen customer penetration and widen its addressable market.
 Operational performance has remained robust. DLPL reported a strong start to FY27, delivering its highest revenue growth in nearly five years, led by healthy test volume growth, improved realization per test and an increasing contribution from specialized diagnostics. Preventive healthcare package Swasthfit continues to gain traction, while Suburban Diagnostics is witnessing improving performance and emerging as an important growth driver in western India. Volume growth has steadily improved over the last two years, reflecting healthy demand trends across geographies. Management remains confident of delivering mid-teen revenue growth in FY27, supported by continued volume momentum, favourable mix and network additions.

Healthy double-digit revenue growth is likely to be driven by strong test volume expansion, higher Swasthfit contribution, benefits from recent CGHS/ECHS price revisions and continued improvement at Suburban. Margins are also expected to remain healthy, supported by operating leverage and a richer test mix.

Street stays bullish on Sun Pharma despite mixed Q2, earnings downgrades
 Analysts remain positive on Sun Pharma despite slower US and speciality growth in Q2FY27, supported by strong domestic sales, though near-term earnings estimates have been cut.
 premium 
 Sun Pharmaceutical Industries reported 12% year-on-year revenue growth to ₹16,200 crore in Q2FY27, but slower speciality and US business growth weighed on near-term earnings prospects, prompting analysts to cut estimates and target prices. (Photo: Re
 Devangshu Datta New Delhi 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 03 2026 | 7:28 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Sun Pharmaceutical Industries (Sun Pharma) had a mixed second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27) where growth in the speciality business and US business slowed, but India growth accelerated. While many analysts continue to be bullish on India’s most valuable pharma company, which closed with a market capitalisation of ₹4.24 trillion on Monday, near-term earnings projections were downgraded along with target prices post-Q2 last Friday. The company’s share price gained initially, but has since given up most of the gains to close at ₹1,768.
 In Q2FY27, revenue beat consensus slightly. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (Ebitda) margin—adjusted for forex gains—was at 28.8 per cent. The domestic business grew 17 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y), while emerging markets (EM) revenue grew 18 per cent and the rest of the world (RoW) 13 per cent. Speciality and innovation were slow.
 Organon’s Q3 was along expected lines, and the acquisition process is on track for completion in early 2027. Sun Pharma had announced Organon’s acquisition in April for an enterprise value of about $12 billion. Operating cash flow (OCF) has grown 26 per cent Y-o-Y in the first nine months (9M) of 2026, with around $3 billion of cash on the balance sheet.
 Sun Pharma’s revenue grew 12 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹16,200 crore. Innovation saw a slowdown since Ilumya’s growth in the US slowed. Illumya is a prescription biologic medication used to treat adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis. The US revenue was $455 million, up $28 million quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q), while speciality revenues (up $5 million Q-o-Q) was lower than expected due to slowdown in Ilumya. Ilumya’s US psoriatic arthritis indication is set for soft launch in November.
 The gross margin was 80.9 per cent, ahead of consensus. Adjusted PAT (profit after tax) grew 1 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹3,160 crore. Excluding generic gRevlimid, Sun Pharma’s revenue increased 15 per cent Y-o-Y, while Ebitda grew 21 per cent. Projections suggest Ilumya’s new psoriatic arthritis FDA label will lead eventually to peak sales of $90-130 million. Sun Pharma and Organon can generate $300 million peak sales in Europe. 
 The company reiterated high single-digit guidance for FY27 (without taking Organon into consideration). Management commentary claims the business outlook remains strong over the medium to long term, with continued traction in the speciality portfolio. But near-term earnings growth will be under pressure due to high marketing expenses on new speciality products and slow US generics performance as well as projected higher R&D expenses in the second half (H2) of FY27.
 Speciality revenue is slow as Ilumya’s growth has slowed down during the quarter. The company says it has taken corrective actions to revive growth but didn't discuss the issues in details. Over the next three years, $450 million incremental revenue is expected through traction in launches and steady traction in base portfolio. Serious revenue contribution from Unloxcyt and Leqselvi to specialty products marketed by Sun Pharma in the US and global markets, will come through in FY28, but FY27 is likely to see the company incur higher spending.
 US generics’ contribution inched up sequentially on five new launches. But the US business may be muted due to regulatory issues across manufacturing plants. Overseas growth may be higher in rupee terms given forex trends. Recent semaglutide approvals in South Africa and Brazil could drive emerging market (EM) revenues.
 Domestic revenue was ₹5,550 crore, up 17 per cent Y-o-Y, with volume growth of 6.5 per cent. Domestic momentum should sustain, given recent field-force expansions, and the ramp-up of semaglutide and new products.
 The Ebitda margin could improve to 30 per cent as specialty products begin to contribute positively. Sun Pharma’s India business contributed 34.5 per cent to its consolidated revenue. It retained market share of 8.6 per cent. Growth initiatives include brand-building, scientific promotion, field-force expansion and increasing prescriber reach. The company launched 15 new products domestically.
 US sales contributed 27 per cent to consolidated sales, with five generics launched. US sales declined 8.2 per cent Y-o-Y due to erosion in lenalidomide revenue. However, US sales were up 6.5 per cent Q-o-Q. EM revenue grew 7.6 per cent Y-o-Y to $350 million and contributed a fifth to revenue. RoW revenue stood at $241 million, higher Y-o-Y, contributing 14.3 per cent to consolidated revenue. Globally, innovative-medicine sales grew 6.9 per cent Y-o-Y to $356 million, accounting for 21.1 per cent of consolidated sales.
 Corrective actions in and psoriatic arthritis launch may restore growth over next few quarters. Ilumya did well in Romania and Brazil. Approximately one-third of psoriasis patients also have psoriatic arthritis, but concrete revenue potential was not discussed. Commercialisation of the arthritis indication will leverage existing sales force, extending coverage beyond dermatologists to rheumatologists. Management confirmed semaglutide commercialisation in India, South Africa, and Brazil.

docs.title: 10 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Motilal Oswal with 21% to 68% upside potential
docs.text: Domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal has a ‘Buy’ rating on stocks across sectors, heavyweights, and mid- and small-caps. In its report dated November 2, 2026, the brokerage has given bullish calls on Reliance Industries, Varun Beverages, Dixon Technologies, Tata Power, and GE Vernova T&D India, among others. The recommendations are based on latest earnings performance and the company’s overall revenue and order visibility. Motilal Oswal recommends ‘Buy’ on Reliance Industries The brokerage has a ‘Buy’ call on the stock with a target price of Rs 1,520 apiece, implying an upside of 21% from the current market price of Rs 1,252.10. The brokerage raised its earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) and net profit outlook for the company by 8-10% for FY27, and by 4-7% for FY28, driven by improved profitability in the energy business and better margin delivery in Jio Platforms. “RIL’s O2C segment is benefitting from dislocations in the energy markets and better capture of elevated product cracks. We expect record-high profitability for O2C in FY27 and then a gradual dip. However, our FY28 O2C EBITDA remains higher than that of the past few years (excluding FY27),” it said. ALSO READFrom inland depots to global ports: 2 stocks chasing a bigger share of India’s trade Motilal Oswal rates Dixon Technologies ‘Buy’ The brokerage has a ‘Buy’ rating on Dixon Technologies (India) with a target price of Rs 15,900 apiece, implying an upside of 29% from the current market price of Rs 12,277. “The company is continuously gaining market share in mobile segment, with strong mobile volumes of 9.7m for the quarter, up 29% QoQ, despite a 16% YoY decline in overall smartphone market volumes in India,” the brokerage said. “Along with this, we have also seen a strong scale-up in IT hardware and Telecom segments, which benefited from product portfolio expansion and higher realization. Weakness was seen on non-mobile segments. We factor in better realization across segments, along with a slight delay in backward integration on displays. We expect FY28 to see full benefit of backward integration and improved volumes from Vivo-JV, exports and new client addition.” it added. The key risks to Motilal Oswal’s outlook would come from lower-than-expected growth in the market opportunity, loss of relationships with key clients, increased competition, and limited bargaining power with clients. Motilal Oswal recommends ‘Buy’ on Varun Beverages The brokerage has a ‘Buy’ rating on Varun Beverages with a target price of Rs 510 apiece, implying an upside of 28% from the current market price of Rs 397.20. It expects the company to deliver healthy performance due to scaling up of operations in international markets, strengthening distribution network domestically and globally, and the scale-up of the snack business, backed by the operationalisation of the Morocco and Zimbabwe markets. It also sees an expanding product portfolio also supporting growth. Motilal Oswal on Tata Power: ‘Buy’ The brokerage has a ‘Buy’ rating on Tata Power with a target price of Rs 442 apiece, implying an upside of 24% from the current market price of Rs 355.20. “The stock has declined 27% over the past six months despite strong FY27 earnings momentum,” it said. Motilal Oswal expects 34% YoY growth in FY27 PAT, led by a sharp reduction in losses at the Mundra plant in Gujarat, and aided by the Section 11 extension and subsequent SPPA framework. Higher earnings from the Indonesian coal business, continued strong profitability at TP Solar backed by over 90% cell utilisation and third-party cell sales, and the commissioning of 2GW of captive renewable energy capacity will also support growth. Motilal Oswal on GE Vernova: ‘Buy’ The brokerage has a ‘Buy’ rating on GE Vernova T&D India with a target price of Rs 5,100 apiece, implying an upside of 23% from the current market price of Rs 4,142.70. “Going ahead, we expect domestic ordering to remain healthy and export orders from parent and non-parent entities to materialize in coming quarters. GVTD is optimistic about the finalization of more HVDC projects over next one year. docs.title: 6 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Jefferies with 34% to 60% upside
docs.text: Dalmia Bharat, Reliance Industries and GMR Airports feature among the stocks that Jefferies have rated 'Buy' in its latest research reports. The recommendations are based on latest earnings performance and the company’s overall revenue and order visibility. The brokerage's cement coverage points to higher selling prices as companies seek to offset rising costs, while its Reliance Industries and Indian Oil Corporation reviews examine the outlook for refining profitability. At GMR Airports, stronger non-aeronautical revenue has supported performance despite weak passenger traffic. 1. Jefferies on Dalmia Bharat: 'Buy' Jefferies has assigned a 'Buy' rating to Dalmia Bharat with a target price of Rs 2,125 against a reported share price of Rs 1,325. This implies upside of approximately 60.4%. Jefferies said cement prices improved in October as manufacturers sought to offset higher input costs. All-India cement prices rose 3.3% month-on-month and 4.3% compared with the previous quarter's average, according to the report. The brokerage expects further price increases to be important as fuel inflation raises costs. It also cautioned that renewed capacity expansion plans by Ambuja Cements have brought competitive intensity back into focus. While the target price makes Dalmia Bharat the highest-upside stock in this ranking, Jefferies' stated sector preference is for Grasim Industries and UltraTech Cement. That distinction is important when describing the brokerage's overall view of the sector. Jefferies wrote, “If 3Q/4Q hikes sustain without meaningful reversals, investor concerns around medium-term capacity additions and competitive intensity should ease, in our view.” 2. Jefferies on Reliance Industries: 'Buy' Jefferies has maintained a 'Buy' rating on Reliance Industries with a target price of Rs 1,710 against a reported share price of Rs 1,164, indicating stated upside of 47% in its November 1, 2026 report. The brokerage said the company's oil-to-chemicals business delivered a strong September-quarter performance, helping earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation exceed its estimates. The retail business, however, fell short of expectations, with festive-season timing and continued investment in quick commerce affecting performance. Jefferies raised its oil-to-chemicals earnings estimates for the 2027 and 2028 financial years, citing the prospect of sustained profitability in the segment during winter. Jefferies wrote, “O2C profitability should be elevated in the winter with damage to refining infrastructure in the Middle East and Russia.” 3. Jefferies on GMR Airports: 'Buy' Jefferies has retained a 'Buy' rating on GMR Airports with a target price of Rs 125, indicating an upside of 44%. Jefferies described the September-quarter performance as soft because passenger traffic remained weak and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation declined 2% year on year. Non-aeronautical revenue nevertheless grew 17% year on year, supported by stronger monetisation at Delhi and Hyderabad airports. ALSO READFrom inland depots to global ports: 2 stocks chasing a bigger share of India’s trade The brokerage also pointed to record yields at these two airports. Platform costs and the integration and ramp-up of new airports weighed on quarterly earnings, while net debt remained stable compared with the previous quarter. Jefferies wrote, “Non-aero revenue was key +ve, growing 17% YoY despite weak pax, with Delhi/Hyderabad delivering record yields.” 4. Jefferies on Ambuja Cements: 'Buy' Jefferies has assigned a 'Buy' rating to Ambuja Cements with a target price of Rs 475, the target implies upside of approximately 36.1%. However, it warned that Ambuja's latest capacity expansion plans had renewed questions about competitive intensity across the industry. Jefferies said price increases would need to hold, with further hikes helping companies manage higher fuel costs. It also noted that pricing trends differed across regions, with stronger increases in the east and gains across several other markets. ALSO READDiwali 2026 stock picks: Mirae Asset Sharekhan names 15 stocks for Samvat 2083 Jefferies wrote, “Ambuja’s latest FY29 capacity expansion plans bring competitive intensity questions back into focus.” 5. Jefferies on Indian Oil Corporation: 'Buy' Jefferies has maintained a 'Buy' rating on Indian Oil Corporation with a target price of Rs 175 against a reported share price of Rs 130, indicating stated upside of 35% in its November 1, 2026 report. The brokerage said reported earnings were substantially ahead of its estimates, supported by stronger refining performance and inventory gains. Refining gross margins reached $18.5 per barrel before accounting for the special additional excise duty, while inventory gains contributed to the quarterly earnings beat. Jefferies wrote, “However, refining is likely to remain strong over the winter on damage to infrastructure and low global inventories.” 6. Jefferies on NTPC: 'Buy' Jefferies has maintained a 'Buy' rating on NTPC with a target price of Rs 425. It indicates an upside of 34%. The brokerage said NTPC's September-quarter profit was 16% above its estimates, aided by lower disincentives, and raised its earnings-per-share estimate for the 2027 financial year by 1%. However, management lowered its guidance for renewable-energy capacity additions in the 2027 financial year to 5 gigawatts from 7 to 8 gigawatts because of transmission delays. Jefferies also reduced its estimate for overall capacity additions during the year to 6 gigawatts from 8.2 gigawatts. Jefferies wrote, “We maintain capacity ramp-up as a key re-rating driver ahead.” Conclusion The biggest upside in Jefferies’ estimates comes with a caveat. The highest target-price upside does not automatically make a stock its favoured sector pick. Across the other recommendations, the key question is whether recent earnings strength can persist despite the risks identified in each rep

docs.text: Global investment bank Jefferies has upgraded its rating on United Spirits to “Buy” from “Hold”. The bank also raised its target price for the stock by nearly 4% to Rs 1,620 apiece. This implies an upside of 20% from the stock’s closing price of Rs 1,346.20 on Monday. Japanese brokerage Nomura retained its “Buy” call on the stock while raising the target price by 6% to Rs 1,700. This reflects an upside of 26%. Both Nomura and Jefferies attributed the positive outlook to growth in volumes and an improving outlook for the second half of FY27. The company’s management remains confident of double-digit P&A value growth for FY27, on a favourable base, easing regulatory headwinds, and the recovery in relaunched McDowell’s, which accounts for almost 60% of its volumes. The free trade agreement between the UK and India has improved the affordability from duties on scotch with J&B relaunched across around 60% of salient markets. Management maintained its double-digit FY27 P&A NSV growth aspiration, aided by Maharashtra normalisation, McDowell’s recovery, premiumisation and innovation,” Jefferies said. Nomura on United Spirits: J&B whiskey relaunch can peak in festive season The brokerage expects volumes to improve as P&A growth will revert to “double digits” in the second half and the full benefit of the festive demand kicks in. The relaunch of the J&B whiskey is also expected to support growth. “J&B whisky relaunched (60% of national salience) as a 100% Scotch at a very attractive price point enabled by FTA, to recruit new consumers and deepen Scotch penetration ahead of peak festive season. Being a Diageo global trademark, it sits within the 10% margin cap,” Nomura said. The company’s trademark vodka, Smirnoff, is growing strongly and is on track for the Rs 1,000 crore net sales value aspiration for FY27. The Smirnoff Ice ready-to-drink will increase consumption occasions and draw from beer and wine and also has a three times multiplier to core brand as drinkers graduate. docs.title: RIL shares surge 8%: Why Jefferies sees 47% upside but Nomura cuts target by 7%
docs.text: The RIL share price has seen sharp gains in morning trade after a steady Q2 performance. Strong refining earnings have improved Reliance Industries' outlook, but retail's struggle to convert growth into higher profits remains a concern. Jefferies sees scope for the stock to recover as energy margins strengthen, while Nomura has lowered its valuation to account for more restrained expectations from some businesses. Reliance Industries' September-quarter performance exposed a growing divide within its business portfolio. Its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) operations benefited from exceptional refining conditions, while retail earnings remained under pressure from the timing of the festive season and continued investment in digital commerce. The contrast has become central to how brokerages assess the company's earnings prospects and valuation. Jefferies believes the market has become too pessimistic about Reliance, leaving room for a recovery as strong energy earnings feed through and retail growth improves. Nomura also sees value in the company, but has adopted a more cautious valuation of retail and exploration and production. The difference is reflected in their price targets. Jefferies has set a target of Rs 1,710, implying 47% upside from its reference price of Rs 1,164. Nomura has reduced its target to Rs 1,560 from Rs 1,690, implying about 34% upside from Rs 1,165. Both retain Buy ratings. Jefferies on RIL: Sees refining strength supporting a recovery Reliance's consolidated EBITDA rose 23% year-on-year to Rs 56,616 crore in the September quarter, beating Jefferies' estimate by 6%. O2C was the main source of the outperformance, with segment EBITDA exceeding the brokerage's estimate, while upstream earnings were also ahead of expectations. ALSO READFrom inland depots to global ports: 2 stocks chasing a bigger share of India’s trade Jefferies' report dated September 2026 points to a favourable refining environment as the main near-term support for earnings. Disruptions to refining infrastructure in the Middle East and Russia have tightened product supplies, while low inventories in key markets have supported refining margins. The brokerage expects these conditions to remain supportive through the winter. It also sees scope for petrochemical spreads to improve as feedstock supplies from the Middle East remain constrained. Jefferies has consequently raised its O2C EBITDA estimates for FY2027 and FY2028, with the improvement lifting its consolidated earnings forecasts. Its broader argument centres on market expectations. Jefferies believes Reliance's valuation has fallen well below its historical range, despite the improved outlook for O2C. If energy earnings remain strong and retail performance improves, the stock could regain some of the valuation it has lost. That recovery, however, depends on more than refining margins alone. Retail needs to demonstrate that its investments in digital commerce and expansion can support sustainable growth without continuing to weigh heavily on profitability. Nomura on RIL: Lowers target as valuation assumptions change Nomura retains a positive view of Reliance but has reduced its price target to Rs 1,560 from Rs 1,690. The revised valuation reflects changes in the multiples assigned to some businesses as the brokerage updates its valuation base. Nomura explained its approach in the report: “We reiterate our Buy rating on RIL with a new sum-of-the-parts (SoTP)-based TP of INR1,560 (vs INR1,690 previously) as we roll forward the valuation base to September 2028.” ALSO READReliance Q2 highlights: Profit up 41%, ‘Jio Platforms is now India’s second largest company,’ says Mukesh Ambani The brokerage uses a sum-of-the-parts approach, valuing Reliance's energy and consumer businesses separately. It lowered the valuation multiple for Reliance Retail to 25 times from 28 times and for exploration and production to five times from six times. Refining and petrochemicals remain valued at 7.5 times forecast EBITDA. The lower retail multiple is particularly relevant given the segment's weak profitability. Retail is one of Reliance's major growth businesses, but its contribution to the group's valuation depends on the company's ability to sustain growth while improving returns. Nomura also assigns separate values to telecom, FMCG, media and new energy. Its assessment therefore recognises Reliance's range of earnings sources, while applying different assumptions to businesses at different stages of maturity. The lower target does not amount to a negative view of the company. Rather, it indicates that Nomura sees less value at present in some businesses than it had previously assumed. The brokerage continues to expect Reliance's portfolio to generate value, but its revised target leaves less room for upside than Jefferies' valuation does. RIL: Retail's growth strategy comes at a cost Retail was the main disappointment in the September quarter. Jefferies reported that EBITDA fell around 11% year-on-year to Rs 5,900 crore, while the margin declined to 7.3%. Festive-season timing affected quarterly comparisons, but the pressure also reflects the costs of building digital channels and competing for customers. The brokerage's commentary captures the tension between the company's growth ambitions and near-term profitability: “Mgmt remains focused on scaling Q/C & defending share, signalling near-term margin pressure, even as it targets profitable growth over time.” That strategy places Reliance Retail in a difficult position. Quick commerce can expand its reach and help it compete in an increasingly demanding market, but building the business requires investment. Store rationalisation and the expansion of digital operations may improve the business over time, yet the immediate effect is pressure on margins. Reliance Retail opened new outlets during the quarter but also rationalised unviable stores, leaving its total store count lower. Jefferies has cut its retail earnings estimates

docs.title: Nomura initiates coverage on Page Industries; sees 24% upside for Jockey India parent
docs.text: The Page Industries share price surged nearly 4% intraday to a high of Rs 35,800 on Monday, November 2. The company’s shares are in focus after Japanese brokerage Nomura initiated coverage on the stock with a ‘Buy’ rating. Nomura has set a target price of Rs 44,000, which implies an upside of 24% from the stock’s current price of Rs 35,500 apiece. Page Industries is the market leader in India’s innerwear segment, but has 18% share in the men’s segment and 7% in the women’s segment, implying “significant headroom” for market penetration. The company is the exclusive licensee for Jockey and Speedo in India. “Our analysis indicates that over the next decade, among the overall households, the addressable market for Jockey’s core (men’s innerwear) should grow the fastest and ahead of overall household growth,” Nomura said. The company is accelerating growth in its whitespaces and higher average selling price products such as women's innerwear and athleisure with new collections like Gen-Z first, JKY Groove, merchandise collection under JKY Studio. This is being done to reinforce its brand relevance among youngsters, expand wallet share, and capture incremental volumes. ALSO READ47% RoE, 4% sales growth: The premium innerwear stock facing a valuation test Nomura on Page Industries: Volume-led growth The brokerage said Page Industries is positioned for a gradual re-acceleration in growth, supported by a growing consumer base, acceleration in youth-focused launches, more realisations per purchase, and more capacity to serve its consumers. The company has guided for double-digit volume growth, which remains the key monitorable. Nomura expects sales growth in the low-teens with low-to-mid-single-digit price growth. The company’s category penetration is only around 18% in men's innerwear and 6-7% each in women's innerwear and athleisure, against a target cohort recording a 6% compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) over the next decade, with over 115,000 retail touchpoints across 2,700 towns that is still mostly skewed to metro or tier-1 cities. This leaves room to grow in tier-2 and tier-3 cities and digital channels. Nomura also expects the company to launch more youth-related products under chief executive officer (CEO) Karthik Y, who took over in April 2025. “Jockey's portfolio is laddered across price tiers, allowing Page Industries to capture consumers transitioning out of unorganised brands and retain them as they upgrade into masstige, where innovationled premiumisation (bonded, performance) converts rising income into mix improvement…” it said. The company also has enough capacity to serve its growing consumer base, with 16 manufacturing facilities. It has a capacity to produce 28 crore pieces, against the 22.8 crore pieces sold in FY26, and is investing ahead of anticipated demand with Odisha and KR Pet facilities. Nomura on Page Industries: Digitisation push The reinstatement of the automated replenishment system (ARS) converted ordering for over 4,800 accounts to system-generated from a sales-force push. The stock keep unit (SKU)-level pulled improved inventory days to 66 from 120 over FY23 to FY26. Working capital days declined to 54 from 75 and gross and EBITDA margins also improved without any price increase. ALSO READTitan to Sky Gold & Diamonds: Which jewellery stocks are poised to gain this Dhanteras? “This lifted ROCE from 50% to 70%+. More importantly, this industry-leading margins are despite Jockey transacting at MRP vs category average discount of 30%. Further, margins being channel/segment agnostic, make an e-comm/q-comm shift neutral, while benefits from operating leverage, digitization (Salesforce distributor management system), sourcing and sewing efficiency will be supportive for margins,” Nomura said. The company plans to keep its margins near the guided range of 19-21%. Page Industries: New categories and deeper penetration The company is poised to gain market share in the key men’s and women’s innerwear segments. New product launches catering to young consumers and a push towards digitisation are expected to support earnings growth. docs.title: Where to invest in November? Axis Securities names 15 stocks across key sectors
docs.text: Diwali is days away, and homes are filling with sweets, lights and new purchases. But what about your portfolio? Oil is costly, foreign investors are selling, and shares are swinging wildly. Where should investors look before the festival lights come on? Axis Securities, a leading brokerage, has just reshuffled its November list of favourite stocks. Two names are in. Two are out. Let’s see which stocks made the cut in Axis Securities’ November list Axis Securities: November market outlook October was a mixed month for Indian equities. The Nifty 50 gained 1.9%, but the broader market struggled. The Nifty Midcap 100 fell 3.04%, while the Nifty Smallcap 250 declined 5.8%. The Nifty 500 was also down 2.9%. According to the brokerage report, the Nifty IT index stood out with a 17.7% rally. However, global conditions remain a concern. Brent crude was approaching $117 per barrel, while the yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond was around 5%. Foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows in the FY26-27 so far were nearing $15 billion. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), meanwhile, had infused around $48 billion into the market. Axis Securities said, “We believe investors should use market corrections to selectively accumulate fundamentally strong businesses rather than attempt to time the market bottom.” ALSO READ315.4% profit growth: This steel PSU trades at a 43% discount to JSW Axis Securities: Two new stocks enter the November portfolio Axis Securities has added LTM and Dr Lal PathLabs, while exiting Dalmia Bharat and Chalet Hotels. According to the brokerage report, rising corporate spending on digital transformation, AI-led solutions and technology modernisation could create opportunities for businesses with strong client relationships and execution capabilities. Dr Lal PathLabs has been added to gain exposure to the diagnostics market. Growing awareness of preventive healthcare and demand for organised testing services are among the factors supporting this choice. The brokerage also points to the company’s established brand and network. Which 15 stocks has Axis Securities picked? The revised November portfolio includes Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bajaj Finance, Bharti Airtel, ICICI Bank, Varun Beverages, APL Apollo Tubes, Healthcare Global Enterprises (HCG), LG Electronics India, Nestle India, Eternal, Dr Lal PathLabs, Minda Corporation, LTM, City Union Bank and CCL Products. Its banking picks provide exposure to credit growth, while Bharti Airtel offers exposure to telecom services. Consumer-facing names such as Varun Beverages, Nestle India and Eternal represent its consumption theme. APL Apollo Tubes and Minda Corporation provide exposure to infrastructure, manufacturing and the automobile industry. LG Electronics India and CCL Products are linked to consumer durables and value-added consumption. HCG and Dr Lal PathLabs add healthcare exposure, while LTM brings a technology-focused business into the portfolio. Which sectors could offer opportunities? Axis Securities is maintaining an overweight stance on banking, telecom, capital goods, industrials, healthcare, pharmaceuticals and select automobile stocks. It also prefers consumer businesses that are reporting volume growth and gaining market share. Within information technology (IT), the brokerage favours select mid-cap companies that could benefit from digital transformation and artificial intelligence-related spending. Its broader investment approach is based on “Growth at a Reasonable Price (GARP)”. The brokerage says its November strategy focuses on “quality, earnings visibility, and valuation discipline”. ALSO READMCX, Groww to SBI Funds: Jefferies names 5 market-linked stocks to play derivatives surge What is the market target for December? Axis Securities has set a December 2026 target of 27,360 for the Nifty. This is based on 19.5 times its estimated earnings for December 2027. The brokerage expects Nifty earnings to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13% between FY22-23 and FY27-28. However, risks remain. Elevated crude prices, geopolitical tension and higher global bond yields could continue to affect market sentiment. The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) 25-basis-point repo rate hike to 5.50% also makes inflation and currency movements important factors to watch. docs.title: Drought, inflation and higher rates: Why Nomura is betting on these 4 NBFC stocks
docs.text: The monsoon deficit is bad news not just for farmers. It also has a ripple effect on banks and lending companies. When rainfall fall is deficient, crop sowing slows and rural income comes under pressure, borrowers may find it harder to repay their loans. Add rising food prices and the possibility of higher interest rates to the mix, and the pressure could extend beyond villages to urban households as well. This is the combination of risks that has put India's non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) under the spotlight. The brokerage house Nomura believes lenders could face a challenging period ahead. The brokerage is not turning cautious on the entire sector. Instead, it is drawing a distinction between lenders exposed to rural and consumption-driven borrowing and those with a larger presence in housing and business loans. According to Nomura, Piramal Finance, Tata Capital, Aadhar Housing Finance and Bajaj Finance are its preferred Buy-rated NBFCs, in that order. The brokerage believes these lenders could be relatively better placed to navigate the current uncertainties. A weak monsoon is becoming a lending-sector concern The first warning sign comes from the weather. India's south-west monsoon ended with a 13% rainfall deficit at the national level, according to Nomura. The South Peninsula, along with eastern and north-eastern regions, recorded rainfall deficits of up to 27%. ALSO READ59.4% profit growth, 68% valuation discount: Meet Bajaj Finance’s smaller rival The impact is beginning to show in agricultural activity. While the Kharif crop sowing season ended with the overall area under cultivation just 1% lower year-on-year, rice sowing was down 3.5%. The start of the Rabi season has been weaker. According to the brokerage report, the area covered under Rabi crops was down 37% year-on-year. Nomura also pointed to falling reservoir levels as another concern. As of October 22, water storage across India was 18% below normal. Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan have declared drought conditions. The brokerage said, "the weather remains unforgiving", highlighting the risks to agricultural activity and rural earnings. Three challenges pose potential challenge for NBFCs The pressure on lenders is not coming from just one direction. Nomura has identified three broad challenges that could affect NBFC performance. First, weaker agricultural conditions could hurt rural incomes and repayment capacity. Second, higher food inflation could leave urban households with less money to spend or repay existing loans. Third, an extended period of higher interest rates could increase borrowing costs and affect lending margins. There are also regulatory concerns around flexible loans and insurance products, which could affect fee income for some lenders. Nomura has created a bearish scenario for the NBFCs under its coverage. It has lowered its loan growth assumptions, increased expected credit costs and reduced estimated insurance fee income by half from FY27-28. The brokerage has also raised its assumed risk-free rate to 7.25% from 6.25%. Under this scenario, Nomura's 12-month fair values indicate a potential downside of 11% to an upside of 27% across the NBFC stocks it covers. Why Nomura is choosing urban-focused lenders over rural players The brokerage prefers companies with a larger share of housing finance, mortgage lending and business loans. These businesses could be relatively less exposed to the pressures facing rural borrowers. On the other hand, lenders with higher exposure to vehicle finance, personal loans and microfinance could face greater uncertainty if weak incomes and higher household expenses affect repayment capacity. ALSO READTitan to Sky Gold & Diamonds: Which jewellery stocks are poised to gain this Dhanteras? Nomura believes it is "better to be selective with NBFCs" until the impact of rural economic conditions and food inflation becomes clearer around November and December 2026. Nomura’s top NBFC stock picks Piramal Finance tops Nomura's preferred NBFC list. The brokerage has placed the lender ahead of the other three stocks in its preferred order. Tata Capital takes the second position in Nomura's list. The brokerage includes the company among its preferred Buy-rated NBFCs as it favours lenders with exposure to urban-focused lending businesses. Aadhar Housing Finance ranks third. Its housing finance business fits into Nomura's preference for lenders with greater exposure to mortgage-related lending rather than rural consumption-driven loans. Bajaj Finance completes the list of four preferred stocks. Nomura has retained the company among its preferred Buy-rated NBFCs. What about other NBFC stocks? Nomura has also identified some lenders that are trading close to its bearish fair-value estimates. These include L&T Finance, Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services, Shriram Housing Finance and HDB Financial Services. The brokerage believes these stocks could see "positive triggers" if asset quality deterioration during the second half of FY26-27 is less severe than assumed in its bearish scenario. It has also highlighted CreditAccess Grameen, noting that the stock is trading at valuation multiples below those seen during the previous crisis, "without any crisis on the ground (yet!)". docs.title: MCX, Groww to SBI Funds: Jefferies names 5 market-linked stocks to play derivatives surge
docs.text: Markets were shaky in October 2026. Prices swung. The Volatility Index (VIX), often called the market’s fear gauge, stayed high. You might expect traders to stay away. Instead, they traded more. Options trading, where people bet on where a price may go next, picked up sharply. So who gains when investors are nervous but active? A recent report by Jefferies examines these changing trends and identifies five preferred stocks in the capital market space, from brokers to mutual fund companies and depositories. Groww, Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), KFin Technologies, SBI Funds Management and Nuvama Wealth Management feature on its list. The global investment banks' assessment comes at a time when equity derivatives activity has picked up, mutual fund flows remain significant and IPO-related activity continues to support the depository business. Here is a detailed analysis of Jefferies' investment rationale - Which capital market stocks feature in Jefferies' preferred list? Jefferies preferred picks include Groww, MCX, KFin Technologies, SBI Funds Management and Nuvama Wealth Management. Higher trading activity puts exchanges in focus The rise in market volatility has brought options trading back into focus. According to the Jefferies report, the average daily turnover (ADTO) of index options premiums stood at Rs 98,700 crore in October 2026, broadly matching March levels. ALSO READ15.4% profit growth: This steel PSU trades at a 43% discount to JSW Trading activity also increased at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and BSE, with their average daily turnover rising 40-50% month-on-month. BSE's share of the options market increased to 35.9% in October from 34.1% in September. However, its cash market share edged lower to 8.3%. Higher trading volumes can support transaction-related income for exchanges. Jefferies believes elevated equity options activity could be positive for NSE and BSE. Groww: More trades, but a slowdown in SIP inflows Equity options contracts traded across the industry increased 28% month-on-month in October, while cash market contracts rose 2%. Groww also recorded a 36% increase in equity derivatives turnover. Jefferies noted that higher selling activity following a major IPO could improve brokers' cash realisation. However, there is another side to the business. The industry's margin trading facility (MTF) book declined 5% month-on-month. Groww's MTF book witnessed a similar fall, partly coinciding with weakness in small- and mid-cap stocks. Its systematic investment plan (SIP) inflows also declined 3% month-on-month in October. According to the report, this was the first monthly fall on Groww's platform since February 2026. Why MCX is benefiting from commodity volatility Commodity market activity offers another investment opportunity. MCX recorded options ADTO of Rs 12,100 crore in October. Although the figure remained flat month-on-month, it was higher than Jefferies' and consensus estimates for the third quarter of financial year 2027. The brokerage said, "Should these trends sustain, it could imply 4-5% upside to our FY27 EPS est." Energy contracts accounted for 68% of MCX's options turnover. Continued volatility in commodity prices could therefore remain an important factor for the exchange's business. ALSO READ6 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Jefferies with 34% to 60% upside SBI Funds Management and KFin Technologies: What is driving interest? The mutual fund industry also saw changes in investor flows. Net equity inflows, excluding arbitrage funds and new fund offers, increased around 30% month-on-month to Rs 42,600 crore in September. Systematic investment plan inflows reached Rs 32,500 crore, marking a fresh high. SBI Funds Management gained market share in equity fund flows during the month. The depository segment, meanwhile, continued to benefit from IPO activity. India saw 18 mainboard IPOs in October, while demat account openings stood at 2.9 million in September. According to Jefferies, Central Depository Services (India) (CDSL) recorded 65% year-on-year growth in IPO and corporate action-related revenue in the September quarter. What next for investors The Jefferies capital market stock picks cover a gamut of stocks across asset management plays, depositories and stock market infra plays. The recommendations are based on the expectations of steady investment interest and the stocks to watch, therein. docs.title: Goldman Sachs raises Brent Dec target to $105: Why $27 risk premium may push oil to $130
docs.text: Goldman Sachs has raised its average Brent crude oil price forecast for 2027 to $88 per barrel from $80, citing risks of supply disruptions in the Middle East and a higher risk premium in oil markets. In its November 1, 2026, commodities research report, the brokerage also raised its West Texas Intermediate (WTI) forecast for 2027 to $78 per barrel from $73. For December 2026, Goldman Sachs increased its Brent forecast to $105 per barrel from $90 and its WTI forecast to $94 per barrel. 1. Goldman Sachs raises Brent and WTI price forecasts Goldman Sachs has increased its crude oil price forecasts as the risk of supply disruptions remains elevated despite the continuing recovery in Middle Eastern output. The brokerage expects the possibility of lower supply to sustain a substantial near-term risk premium, while its revised global supply assumptions account for disruption risks over the medium term. The report states, "Although Mideast output continues to recover as expected, we are raising our crude oil price forecasts because substantial downside supply risks are likely to sustain a large near-term risk premium, while our new global supply disruption allowance captures high disruption risk over the medium term." Goldman Sachs has raised its December 2026 Brent forecast to $105 per barrel from $90 and its WTI forecast to $94 per barrel. For the 2027 annual average, the brokerage now expects Brent to reach $88 per barrel, compared with its earlier estimate of $80, while its WTI forecast has increased to $78 per barrel from $73. 2. Higher risk premium drives the crude oil rally Goldman Sachs estimates that the increase in the risk premium to around $27 explains most of October's crude oil price rally. The brokerage said Brent crude's estimated fair value changed little during September and October, as global inventories remained broadly stable while oil production and consumption adjusted. The report states, "A jump in the risk premium to around $27 now explains most of October’s crude price rally." Goldman Sachs expects the market to price in a higher risk premium because of potential disruptions to Middle Eastern supply, the duration of past major oil supply shocks and the difficulty of achieving a lasting diplomatic breakthrough. ALSO READ4x oil production target by FY30: An under-the-radar smallcap betting on bigger profits The brokerage's analysis distinguishes between the movement in crude oil prices caused by supply and demand fundamentals and the additional premium associated with geopolitical risks. Its assessment indicates that the recent rally has largely reflected concerns about possible disruptions rather than a substantial change in global inventories. 3. Middle East and Russia-Ukraine conflicts raise supply risks Goldman Sachs said the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, alongside broader geopolitical fragmentation, have increased the risk of supply disruptions. Since the timing and location of potential disruptions are difficult to predict, the brokerage has incorporated a 1 mb/d global supply disruption allowance into its 2027 base case. The report states, "With the timing and location of disruptions nearly impossible to predict, our base case now includes a 1mb/d global supply disruption allowance in 2027." Despite the reduction in projected global supply, Goldman Sachs expects its base-case price forecasts to remain somewhat below forward prices. This assessment assumes that the elevated risk premium moderates and Persian Gulf production continues its gradual recovery. The brokerage's revised outlook therefore accounts for potential supply losses while retaining its expectation that the recovery in Gulf production will continue. ALSO READIndia’s inflation risks rise as crude oil, shipping costs threaten to push up prices 4. Brent crude could reach $140 per barrel in 2027 Goldman Sachs expects Brent crude prices to reach $140 per barrel and average around $130 per barrel in 2027 under its upside case. This outcome assumes that average Gulf oil production in 2027 remains 3.5 mb/d below its 2025 average, compared with the brokerage's base-case assumption of production being 1.1 mb/d above the 2025 average. The report states, "The most likely price upside triggers are intensified shipping attacks, damage to oil infrastructure, and a more persistent risk premium." The upside case reflects the possibility that geopolitical tensions could restrict oil supplies more severely than assumed in the base case. Intensified attacks on shipping, damage to oil infrastructure and a persistent risk premium could combine to push Brent crude prices significantly higher. Goldman Sachs has retained an upward bias in its assessment of price risks, even as it considers the potential for prices to move in either direction more balanced than before. 5. Brent crude could fall into the $60s if Gulf output recovers faster Goldman Sachs has also outlined a downside case in which Brent crude prices decline into the $60s in 2027. This assumes that average Gulf oil production rises 2.5 mb/d above its 2025 level and that the disruption included in the brokerage's global supply allowance does not occur. Under these conditions, higher production would increase available supply, while a faster decline in the risk premium would ease the pressure on prices. The report identifies the most likely downside triggers as "a faster recovery in Mideast output and/or a faster decline in the risk premium." This outcome contrasts with the upside case, in which Brent could reach $140 per barrel. The difference between the two cases illustrates the extent to which the brokerage's oil price outlook depends on the recovery in Gulf production and the duration of geopolitical risks. Goldman Sachs retains upward bias in oil price outlook Goldman Sachs said risks to its crude oil price forecasts have become more balanced but continue to favour higher prices overall. Its base case assumes that Persian Gulf production continue

docs.title: When will FIIs return? Leading Indian broker has a timeline
docs.text: Foreign funds are unlikely to return to Indian stocks in a big way until crude oil falls, according to JM Financial, a leading Indian broker. Cheap valuations alone haven't been enough to stop the $64 billion exit. The brokerage says FIIs sold $59.2 billion of Indian equities in the 24 months to September 2026. Adding roughly $5 billion sold in October so far, as per press reports, takes the total to about $64 billion. The outflow over the 12 months to June hit a record $40 billion. Since 2016, FIIs sold in six of the seven months when Brent averaged above $105 a barrel, pulling out $4.1 billion a month on average. JM Financial says that below about $90 they stop selling. Brent was $114.6 on 27 October. The report says the US midterm elections on 3 November and the path of the Iran conflict decide the timing. The brokerage house has given a 45% chance to a base case in which Brent stays between $100 and $115 and the first three straight inflow months arrive in January to March 2027. It gives 25% to a faster recovery and 30% to escalation. JM Financial maps 3 possible scenarios to attract FII flows JM Financial ties its flow estimates to developments in the US-Iran conflict. It says the probabilities and ranges are its own judgement and not model output. In its base case, muddle-through at 45%, strikes and attacks are episodic, talks stop and start and Brent stays between $100 and $115, capped by mediation. Valuation supports, but oil caps, and the first three-month inflow run comes in January to March 2027. De-escalation, at 25%, has talks resuming after 3 November, shipping attacks falling, and Hormuz normalising. Brent falls to $85 to $90 by the first quarter of 2027, which pulls the first inflow run forward to December 2026 and January 2027. The report also assumes EPS upgrades, capital gains tax relief in the February 2027 Budget, and a P/E above 20 times. Escalation, at 30%, includes US strikes on Iran after the vote, Hormuz closing again, and the Houthi-Saudi conflict widening, with Brent at $125 to $140 for some months. The report assumes the P/E falls below 16 times and first inflows move into FY28. ALSO READWhy FIIs sharply raised stakes in these 3 stocks When will FIIs return: JM Financial charts potential roadmap PathProbabilityOil and geopolitical assumptionsRecovery timingFY27E flowsFY28E flowsDe-escalation25%Talks resume after 3 Nov, mediation holds, Hormuz normalises. Brent $85–90 by Q1 2027, $70–80 by late 2027First inflow run pulled forward to Dec 2026–Jan 2027About –$8bn+$20–25bnMuddle-through (base case)45%Episodic strikes and attacks, talks stop and start, Brent capped by mediation at $100–115Jan–Mar 2027About –$18bn+$10–15bnEscalation30%US strikes on Iran after the vote, Hormuz closes again. Brent $125–140 for some monthsFirst inflows move into FY28About –$28bnAbout –$10bn Source: JM Financial estimates. FY27E includes the $12.7 billion sold in April to September. A record selling spell, with little sign of sustained return According to JM Financial, FIIs sold $14.9 billion in FY25, $21.9 billion in FY26 and $17.7 billion so far in FY27, including October. The longest earlier run of selling in its data was two years. March 2026, at $14.2 billion, is the largest month on record. Only 5 of the last 12 months saw net inflows. September's $4.1 billion outflow undid the July and August inflows of $2.5 billion and $2.4 billion. Since July 2022, FIIs have sold $51.5 billion in the secondary market while buying $36.3 billion in primary issues and other off-market deals. The report says, "They are selling what is already listed." Domestic institutions bought $91.7 billion over the last 12 months. FII ownership of Indian equities fell from 19.9% of market capitalisation in March 2016 to 14.2% in June 2026, while domestic institutions went from 11.3% to 18.9%. India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets index fell from 20.0% in July 2024 to 10.7% in September 2026, which the report says lowers the structural flow. ALSO READGoldman Sachs raises Brent Dec target to $105: Why $27 risk premium may push oil to $130 Why India's growth and earnings recovery have not been enough The report calls the standard explanation that foreign money follows GDP growth, carry and earnings growth. Its data does not support the growth part. Flows correlate at negative 0.11 with GDP growth and at negative 0.32 with growth two quarters earlier. The brokerage does not read the lagged figure as causal and says it would not lean on it with about 20 quarters per regime, but adds: "The sign is the opposite of the growth thesis." In the June 2020 quarter, GDP growth was negative 23.1%, and FIIs bought $4.2 billion. In the March 2026 quarter, GDP grew 8.6%, and FIIs sold $15.8 billion, the largest quarterly outflow in the data. The India-US interest rate gap has a small positive link with flows, at 0.18 for the full period. It narrowed to 2.0 percentage points in September 2026 against an average of 4.9 points over 2006 to 2020, which the report calls a headwind for a return of flows but not a trigger. Earnings growth correlates at only 0.05 with flows. Nifty50 EPS grew 3.2% in FY25 and 5.0% in FY26, then profit rose 12.9% in the June 2026 quarter against the brokerage's expectation of 4.5%. It expects 20.6% for the September quarter. A return of earnings growth removes a reason to sell, the report says, but the rupee and oil decide how much of the rupee growth reaches dollar returns. "We therefore treat the earnings recovery as supportive, not as the trigger." Cheaper valuations could lead to inflows, but with a lag JM Financial measures valuation through the earnings yield, which is 100 divided by the one-year forward price-to-earnings ratio. It finds no same-month link with flows but a positive link four to five months later and a stronger one with the next 12 months of flows. "A cheap market does not draw money immediately," the report says. When the Nifty started a 12-month window below 21 times forward

docs.title: From inland depots to global ports: 2 stocks chasing a bigger share of India’s trade
docs.text: India’s container opportunity is more than just making shipping boxes. The country is developing a connected ecosystem of container production, rail transport, ports and shipping. Indian Shipping Container Market is expected to reach $361.6 million in FY25 and is projected to grow to $881.5 million by FY34 at a CAGR of 10.4%. Meanwhile, the major ports handled 915.17 million tons of cargo in FY26, Indian Railways transported 1,670 million tons of freight and global container-port throughput exceeded an estimated 1 billion twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in 2025. For readers: Two companies that offer different entry points into this developing ecosystem are CONCOR and Adani Ports. #1 CONCOR: The Rail-Linked Logistics Network Connecting India's Factories With Its Ports Container Corporation of India (CONCOR) is a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Railways, primarily engaged in transporting containers by rail and providing integrated logistics services. Its business covers inland container depots (ICDs), container freight stations, multimodal logistics parks, warehousing, port connectivity and first-mile and last-mile transportation. This makes CONCOR an important link between India's manufacturing centres and maritime gateways. Unlike a conventional freight operator, it combines transportation infrastructure with container-handling assets, allowing it to participate in several stages of an export-import (EXIM) shipment. The Inland Network Is CONCOR's Biggest Competitive Asset CONCOR has 68 terminals, including logistics parks, more than 15 logistics parks and 422 wagons. Its network connects inland industrial centres such as Dadri, Ludhiana, Kanpur and Tughlakabad with important western and eastern ports, including Mundra, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now CONCOR's container procurement programme also connects it with India's domestic manufacturing ambitions. Under the Make in India initiative, the company had placed orders for 21,620 indigenously manufactured containers. The company currently has a fleet of 56,008 containers. The distinction between container procurement and container manufacturing is important. CONCOR purchases containers to support its logistics operations; it is not itself the principal manufacturer in this segment. Its returns therefore depend on how efficiently the additional equipment is deployed. Specialised Cargo Opens Another Route To Revenue CONCOR is also widening the range of goods that can be transported through its network. In its Q1 FY26, CONCOR introduced specialised tank containers for transporting bulk cement and customer-owned tank containers for bulk liquids. It also reported the movement of industrial chemicals in tank containers from Paradip Port to Dadri and Khatuwas. Customer-owned equipment can be particularly useful because CONCOR may provide transportation and network access without financing every specialised container itself. Another important development is rail connectivity for the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal at Varnama, linked to the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) through New Makarpura Yard. Two Wagon Orders Strengthen The Transportation Backbone In October, CONCOR placed an ₹87.15 crore order with Southern Railway for 12 rakes of BLSS wagons. A few days later, it placed another order worth ₹485.93 crore with Braithwaite & Co. Ltd. for 24 rakes of BLSS wagons with Brake Van Type BVCM. The delivery deadline for the latter order is 20 June 2028. More rakes can handle more transportation capacity. They can also help CONCOR run more routes, given sufficient cargo demand and railway access. Bharat Container Shipping Line Could Extend CONCOR's Reach To The Sea Another development concerning the integrated container-chain theme is the proposed Bharat Container Shipping Line (BCSL). The Shipping Corporation of India, CONCOR, Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority, V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority, Chennai Port Authority and Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited signed a Memorandum of Understanding in February 2026 to establish BCSL. The proposed initiative is to connect the major ports of India with the inland markets through development of a domestic container shipping ecosystem. It is intended to strengthen end-to-end logistics, improve freight-cost stability and reduce dependence on foreign shipping operators. Q1 FY27: The Revenue Engine Holds, But Growth Remains on Track Two CONCOR reported a largely stable consolidated revenue performance in Q1 FY27, with growth in EXIM logistics offset by a decline in domestic logistics. The results matter to the integrated container-chain investment theme because they show whether rising freight volumes are translating into higher revenue and profit. ParticularsQ1 FY27Year-on-year changeRevenue from operations₹2,159.76 crore0.28%Total income₹2,245.26 crore(0.16%)Total expenses₹1,885.15 crore(0.77%)Profit before tax₹360.11 crore3.17%Profit after tax before share of joint ventures₹272.46 crore5.14%Consolidated profit for the period₹268.90 crore0.61% Revenue grew only marginally, but lower total expenses helped improve profit before tax. EXIM growth offsets domestic weakness: SegmentQ1 FY27 revenueChangeEXIM logistics₹1,433.65 crore2.33%Domestic logistics₹726.11 crore(3.53%) EXIM logistics generated approximately 66.4% of consolidated operating revenue, while domestic logistics contributed 33.6%. This mix makes CONCOR's performance sensitive to international trade flows, port evacuation and export-import demand. The decline in domestic revenue also shows that the benefits of network expansion were not uniform across its business segments. ALSO READ2 defence smallcaps with up to 81% ROCE.
