docs.title: 200% revenue growth, 14X profit: 2 niche stocks riding the global data centre boom
docs.text: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving new demand for data centre infrastructure. As companies deploy more powerful chips and expand computing capacity, server racks generate more heat than conventional air-cooling systems can handle efficiently. This is pushing data centres towards liquid cooling solutions. At the same time, running these facilities around the clock is increasing demand for reliable, on-site power sources, including solid oxide fuel cells. This shift is creating new opportunities for Indian manufacturers supplying the global data centre industry. This article discusses two companies. Both companies have reported their Q2FY27 results, with strong year-on-year growth in revenue and net profit. One company recorded 200% revenue growth and a nearly 14-fold increase in net profit. The other reported 87% revenue growth and a 156.8% rise in net profit. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now One of them manufactures fuel cell components for Bloom Energy and is also collaborating with SLB on data centre infrastructure solutions. The other company supplies liquid cooling systems to a leading American technology firm. Let's take a look. #1 MTAR Technologies: The Primary Vendor for Bloom Energy MTAR Technologies' Data Centre Infrastructure Solutions business vertical sits under its broader Clean Energy segment. This vertical aims to leverage MTAR's precision engineering capabilities to address the global build-out of data centre infrastructure. MTAR has partnered with the global engineering company SLB (Schlumberger) as its primary client in this segment. It has received an initial 'first-article qualification' order worth ₹45 crore from SLB, which is currently being executed. The order is expected to be delivered within six months. MTAR Capacity Expansion: Scaling SLB & Bloom Energy Orders To scale production, MTAR is establishing a dedicated production base. The plan is to establish the initial facility and complete preparations for Phase 1 by mid-December 2026. The facility is expected to become fully operational by the end of March 2027. Phase 2 of the facility expansion is expected to be ready by June 2027. After successfully delivering the initial order, SLB reported a demand pipeline 8x the original order value. Management projects the Data Centre Infrastructure Solutions vertical to clock revenue of ₹350-₹450 crore over the next 2 years by FY29. MTAR Clean Energy Order Book: Solid Oxide Fuel Cell Order Book Growth to ₹5,976.5 crore MTAR is also a long-term partner (15+ years) of Bloom Energy. It develops and supplies core components for Solid Oxide Fuel Cell technology. Fuel cells provide a clean, reliable energy source directly on site. It is the largest portion of MTAR's Clean Energy vertical. The product accounts for 67.2% of the ₹5,976.5 crore order book as of September 30, 2026. MTAR manufactures and supplies complete 'hot box' assemblies and the related components for Bloom’s Energy. MTAR delivers the hot box as a fully integrated assembly. Over the past few years, MTAR has indigenized a significant portion of the sub-components and motors used within these units. MTAR is one of two primary global suppliers for Bloom Energy's hot box assemblies (alongside a South Korean manufacturer). To meet growing fuel cell demand, MTAR is expanding its capacity. The Phase 2 expansion will increase existing capacity by 30%. The facility will be operational by the end of November 2026. The third phase is targeted for completion by March 2027. Out of MTAR's total budgeted capex of ₹500 crore over two years, ₹350 crore (70%) is earmarked for its fuel cell business. The key point is that orders for 'hot box assembly' keep coming in, and currently demand is higher than supply capacity. MTAR Q2FY27 Earnings: EBITDA Margins Hit 24.4% Management has set an 80% year-on-year revenue growth target for FY27 (from ₹876 crore in FY26). MTAR has already achieved 48.7% of the target (₹767.5 crore) in H1FY27. In H1FY27, its revenue grew by 162.7% year-on-year to ₹767.5 crore. In Q2FY27, revenue increased by 200% year-on-year to ₹406.8 crore. H2FY27 is expected to be stronger than H1, driven by capacity additions and accelerated order execution. In Q2FY27, EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) rose 483.3% to ₹99.2 crore as the margin nearly doubled from 12.5% in Q2FY26 to 24.4%. Net profit grew almost 14X to ₹59.8 crore from a low base of ₹4.4 crore in Q2FY26. ALSO READRs 2.8 lakh cr data centre boom: 2 stocks powering AI without making a single chip The company generated ₹350 crore in operating cash, supported by higher profits and customer advances. Inventory control and improved collections reduced net working capital days from 172 days in March 2026 to 50 days in September 2026. Management aims to bring the full-year number to 100 days by the end of FY27. MTAR Share Price #2 Aeroflex Industries: The Cooling Vendor for US Tech Giants Aeroflex Industries manufactures metallic flexible flow solutions. The company produces industrial hardware that moves liquids and gases safely under pressure, heat or movement. Aeroflex has built a specialised product segment focused on AI data centres. Modern artificial intelligence chips run dense computing loads that generate extreme heat. Standard air cooling can no longer remove heat from these servers efficiently. Aeroflex builds liquid cooling skid assemblies and secondary fluid networks. These systems circulate liquid coolants directly to server racks without fluid leaks. Aeroflex supplies these cooling units under an exclusive agreement with a leading American technology firm in India. The company plans to supply liquid cooling products to international markets. docs.title: 3 private banks growing loans faster than HDFC Bank—At up to a 58% discount
docs.text: The domestic economy has been broadly resilient despite the broadly deficient monsoon this year coupled with no signs of a solution to the Middle East crisis and the Russia and Ukraine war. This broad momentum has been reflected in strong demand for autos, broadly resilient demand for housing and buoyant GST tax collections for the government. The government is expected to release second quarter of FY27 data on November 30. To leverage the broad growth momentum in the economy, bank stocks are once again in focus. However, one needs to look beyond the well-known large private sector banks, on account of valuations and moderate returns over the past few years (view table below). FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now For instance, HDFC Bank ended 1% higher at Rs 699.5 on Monday, and it is hovering above its 52-week low of Rs 668.9 that was reached on 28 October, 2026. We searched mid-cap private banks with a market capitalisation of less than Rs 10,000 crore. We then looked at the performance of mid-cap banks on various operational parameters – loan growth, net interest margin (NIM), deposit growth and asset quality (view table below) and then compared them to HDFC Bank. Here are our findings. The Regional Edge: Defending NIMs in a Soft Rate Cycle Mid-cap banks often operate in certain states / regions and with a strong emphasis on lending to high-margin gold loans, SME and retail loans. This lending strategy broadly helped mid-cap private banks to overcome the ‘soft’ interest environment followed by RBI up to the end of the second quarter of FY27. Also, since these mid-cap banks often focus on a few states / regions they understand customers better vis-à-vis leading private sector banks like HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank. The mid-cap banks have grown their loan book by double-digits in the September 2026 quarter, which is a ‘slack’ season for credit, and in many cases grown their loan book faster than HDFC Bank (view table below). The growth in loan books for mid-cap banks has come at a time when the monsoon has been broadly weak this year coupled with no signs of easing in the Middle East crisis. However, it needs to be recognised that the loan books of mid-cap banks is a small fraction of HDFC Bank. ALSO READ59.4% profit growth, 68% valuation discount: Meet Bajaj Finance’s smaller rival Dhanlaxmi Bank: The Gold Loan Strategy Driving a 109% Profit Surge Kerala-based Dhanlaxmi Bank’s loan book grew by a buoyant 23.1% y-o-y Rs 15,738 crore in the quarter. Once again, the bank has aggressively grown high-margin loans – gold loans grew a healthy 53.4% y-o-y to Rs 6,823 crore in the quarter, according to its investor presentation, while SME loans grew by 35.9 % y-o-y to Rs 2,544 crore. As a result, its NIM was 3.6% as compared to 3.25% a year earlier. Asset quality of Dhanlaxmi Bank was also good – its % of net NPAs to net advances was 0.45% as compared to 1.12% a year earlier. However, its provisions were Rs 5.69 crore as compared to Rs 4.99 crore a year earlier. CSB and DCB Bank: Asset Quality Wins and the 142% Gold Loan Outlier Kerala-based CSB Bank’s loan book grew by a healthy 22.2% y-o-y to Rs 41,851.6 crore in the quarter, and that was thanks to high-margin gold loans that grew 35.5% y-o-y to Rs 22,303 crore. CSB Bank in its results presentation has highlighted that gold loans accounted for 53% of its gross advances mix as compared to 47% a year earlier. Its NIM was 3.8% and broadly similar to a year earlier. Asset quality of CSB Bank was also good – its % of net NPAs was 0.33% as compared to 0.5% a year earlier. Provisions also came down substantially – they were Rs 30 crore as compared to Rs 63.6 crore a year earlier. As a result, CSB Bank’s net profit grew 14% y-o-y to Rs 182.7 crore in the quarter. DCB Bank – 142.3% growth in gold loans Mumbai-based DCB Bank’s loan book grew by 21% y-o-y to Rs 64,126.6 crore in the quarter, and that was led by gold loans that grew 142.3% y-o-y to Rs 7,254 crore while corporate loans grew 42.7% y-o-y to Rs 5,379 crore. Its NIM was 3.25% and broadly similar to a year earlier. Asset quality of DCB Bank was also good – its % of net NPAs to net advances was 0.73% as compared to 1.21% a year earlier. Provisions were broadly stable – Rs 64.5 crore as compared to Rs 60.5 crore a year earlier. Strong growth in loans helped DCB Bank’s net profit rise 28.5% y-o-y to Rs 236.4 crore in the quarter. The RoE Reality Check: Efficiency vs. Pure Scale Dhanlaxmi Bank has a return of equity (RoE) of 7.15%, according to Screener.in, 13.5% for CSB Bank and 12% for DCB Bank. HDFC Bank has a standalone RoE of 14%. docs.title: AI Boom vs Jobs: Microsoft voluntary exit plan signals Big Tech shift
docs.text: Big Tech is confronting an uncomfortable question amid its artificial intelligence (AI) boom: can companies become more productive with fewer people? As billions of dollars flow into data centres, chips and AI applications, technology companies are reassessing workforce sizes, hiring plans and the skills they need. Microsoft’s voluntary exit programme has brought this shift into focus, as AI redraws the boundaries between technology, productivity and jobs.The programme, described by executive vice-president and chief people officer Amy Coleman as a new approach to managing organisational change, offers eligible employees financial support and career-planning resources to leave the company. Around 60,000 employees globally are eligible, including those in India, the US, the UK and Canada. Microsoft has approximately 23,000 employees in India, though it has not disclosed how many qualify. Employees must decide by December 1.Coleman said the initiative gives employees considering opportunities outside Microsoft “a new choice to make that transition now with support”. The company has not explicitly linked the programme to AI replacing jobs. Its timing, however, raises a larger question: is AI making Big Tech smaller, or changing what a technology company looks like?The scale of workforce restructuring suggests the shift is already underway. Amazon eliminated 16,000 corporate jobs early this year, following 14,000 cuts in October 2025. Oracle has reportedly cut around 21,000 positions in 2026, while Meta announced plans to eliminate 8,000 jobs and leave thousands of vacancies unfilled. Cisco, too, has undertaken workforce reductions.Not every cut is driven by AI. Cost pressures, organisational complexity and changing business priorities are also at play. Yet as companies redirect billions towards AI, they face growing pressure to improve productivity, simplify management structures and generate returns on their investments.Jaspreet Bindra, founder and CEO of AI&Beyond and Tech Whisperer, sees a shift from headcount growth to “capability density” - getting more work done with smaller, more specialised teams. Routine coding, testing, reporting and coordination can increasingly be automated, allowing fewer employees to deliver comparable output.The difference in productivity between established technology giants and newer AI companies offers a glimpse of where the industry could be headed. “Anthropic makes $6 million+ per employee, Microsoft is a few hundred thousand dollars per employee. Big Tech companies are shrinking to work in a way similar to the new AI labs,” Bindra says. ALSO READApple doubles down on the desk, Anthropic files for an IPO, and the rest of tech goes ambient The comparison points to a different model of growth, in which revenue and output matter more than the number of people on the payroll. Microsoft, meanwhile, is investing approximately $170 billion in capital expenditure during calendar year 2026, with the vast majority directed towards AI infrastructure, data centres and advanced chips. “Headcount will no longer proxy for ambition; output per employee will increasingly define overall scale in the future,” Bindra says.For India, the implications could be particularly far-reaching. The IT services has traditionally relied on a pyramid-shaped workforce, with large numbers of fresh graduates handling coding, testing, maintenance and support under experienced professionals.AI threatens to narrow this base. If a smaller team using AI tools can complete work that once required several junior employees, demand for freshers could weaken even as companies seek more specialised talent.Sachin Grover, vice-president and head of GenAI initiatives at NIIT, says professionals will increasingly need to build, integrate, validate and govern AI-enabled solutions rather than simply execute predefined tasks. Problem-solving, critical thinking and the ability to use AI tools effectively will become essential alongside technical knowledge.India has significant advantages, accounting for 28% of the world's STEM workforce and 23% of global software engineering talent. But the size of its talent pool alone cannot guarantee employment if entry-level work changes faster than education and training can adapt.Manish Prasad, president and managing director of SAP Indian Subcontinent, says preparing Indian talent for the next wave of innovation requires sustained investment in how people learn and apply their skills. SAP aims to equip two million people in India with AI-ready skills by 2030, contributing to its global target of 12 million. Nearly 13% of its India target has already been reached through certification, student education and community programmes, the company said. ALSO READLessons from Binance hack: 7 steps crypto investors should take to protect their money Yet it would be misleading to interpret every layoff as evidence of AI eliminating jobs. Companies are also correcting earlier hiring excesses and responding to changing business conditions. Meanwhile, AI is creating opportunities in model development, chip design, data infrastructure, cybersecurity, governance and enterprise implementation. The question is whether these roles will grow fast enough to offset pressure on routine work, and whether displaced employees can acquire the skills needed to move into them.For Big Tech, the reset is about getting more out of fewer people as computing power takes on a growing share of the work. For India's IT industry, the challenge is more immediate: its traditional employment engine must adapt before the entry-level jobs it has long generated become harder to find.The AI boom may create enormous wealth and new categories of work. But unless those gains translate into broader employment opportunities, the industry risks building the future with fewer people while leaving a generation of aspiring technology workers wondering where they fit in.

docs.title: D-Street cheers RIL Q2, easing oil prices: Sensex soars 1,200 points, Nifty tops 23,400
docs.text: The Indian equity benchmarks had a terrific start to the week, with market sentiment improving due to falling crude oil prices, good quarterly results by heavyweights such as Reliance Industries, and early signs of a return of foreign investors. The Sensex ended 1,233.25 points higher, or 1.66%, at 75,692.78 points on Monday, November 2. The Nifty ended 387.70 points higher, or 1.68%, at 23,440.80 points. Reliance Industries ended the day with 11.6% gains, followed by Tata Steel with 5.8% and JSW Steel with 5.1% gains. Shriram Finance and Coal India surged nearly 5% each. On the other hand, Infosys closed 2% lower. Several banking stocks such as ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and Axis Bank also closed 0.7% lower each. ALSO READFrom inland depots to global ports: 2 stocks chasing a bigger share of India’s trade Drivers of the rally “Indian equities opened the week on a firm footing, supported by better than estimated Q2 earnings and improving domestic cues. Domestic macro indicators provided an additional boost to sentiment with October passenger-vehicle sales growth reflecting healthy festive demand, while gross GST collections increased, reinforcing the resilience of domestic consumption and economic activity,” Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments said in a note. Global cues were also supportive, as crude oil prices eased from six-month highs, with Brent falling below $110 per barrel from around $116 per barrel last week. “Foreign investors turning buyers as a global AI rotation also provided support to domestic equities. The rally extended to the broader market, with mid- and small-cap indices also advancing, indicating an improvement in market participation,” Nair added. Energy, metals, and auto stocks were the key gainers on Monday while IT and pharmaceutical stocks ended mostly flat. The Oil and Gas Index was the outperformer on Monday, surging nearly 6%. The Nifty Metal index also jumped over 3%. Broader market indices also gained, with the Nifty Midcap 150 closing over 1% higher and the Nifty Smallcap 250 ending 1.4% higher. Sensex, Nifty: Key levels to watch “Technically, the market opened with a gap up and maintained positive momentum throughout the day. A bullish candle on the daily charts and an uptrend continuation pattern on the intraday charts indicate further upside from current levels,” Shrikant Chouhan, Head Equity Research at Kotak Neo said in a note. Chouhan said the short-term trend is positive and buying on dips and selling on rallies would be the ideal strategy for day traders. ALSO READ10 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Motilal Oswal with 21% to 68% upside potential The key support levels are now 23,300 and 23,200 for Nifty 50 and 75,300 and 75,000 for Sensex. On the upside, the trend could continue towards 23,500-23,650 and 76,000-76,150. “However, below 23200/75000, the uptrend would become vulnerable, and traders may prefer to exit their long positions,” he added. What investors should watch now? Indian equity markets are likely to remain constructive in the near term as long as crude oil prices are contained. However, a few positive sessions are not enough to confirm a reversal of the recent downtrend, analysts said. investors will remain watchful of the outcome of the US midterm elections on November 3. Stock specific action is likely to remain in the coming days as several companies release their quarterly results.

docs.title: Stocks to watch on Nov 3: ITC, Marico, Petronet LNG, TBO Tek, and more
docs.text: The Indian equity benchmarks rallied on Monday on improving market sentiment due to easing crude oil prices. The Reliance Industries share price ended over 11% higher after posting firm results for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27). The Sensex ended 1,233.25 points higher, or 1.66%, at 75,692.78 points on Monday, November 2. The Nifty ended 387.70 points higher, or 1.68%, at 23,440.80 points. The shares of the following companies will remain in focus on November 3: ITC The company’s net profit declined 20.1% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 4,137 crore from Rs 5,176 crore a year ago. ITC’s revenue, excluding excise duty, rose marginally by 1.8% to Rs 18,401 crore from Rs 18,081 crore a year ago. Its earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) fell 17.5% to Rs 5,160 crore and EBITDA margin contracted 660 basis points to 28%. ALSO READFrom inland depots to global ports: 2 stocks chasing a bigger share of India’s trade Marico Consumer goods firm Marico posted its Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit at Rs 550 crore, rising 31% year-on-year from Rs 420 crore, reported in the same quarter last year. However, sequentially, the company’s bottom line contracted by 13% from Rs 630 crore in Q1 FY27. The company, which operates brands like Parachute and Saffola, reported a 13% YoY jump in its revenue from operations for the July-September quarter at Rs 3,897 crore. During the same quarter last year, its revenue stood at Rs 3,450 crore. Petronet LNG Petronet LNG reported a standalone net profit of Rs 1,235.4 crore for Q2FY27, up 9.1% sequentially. Its revenue from operations rose 29.6% sequentially to Rs 7,200 crore for the quarter. The company’s EBITDA rose 8.6% to Rs 1,663 crore from Rs 1,532 crore in the previous quarter. However, its EBITDA margin contracted to 23% from 28%. NMDC The iron-ore major posted its quarterly business update. NMDC’s total iron ore production rose to 5.04 million tonnes in October, up 18% YoY. However, its sales fell around 12% to 3.44 million tonnes from 3.89 million tonnes. For April-October, the state-owned company’s iron production rose 22% to 32.32 million tonnes while sales fell nearly 2% to 25.67 million tonnes. CONCOR Container Corporation of India reported a net profit of Rs 353 crore for Q2FY27, down nearly 7% YoY. Its revenue from operations rose marginally by 1% to Rs 2,379 crore from Rs 2,355 crore a year ago. CONCOR’s EBITDA fell 4.5% to Rs 550 crore and EBITDA margin contracted to 23% from 25% a year ago. ALSO READ10 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Motilal Oswal with 21% to 68% upside potential TBO Tek TBO Tek’s net profit for Q2FY27 rose 12.6% YoY to Rs 76 crore from Rs 67.5 crore a year earlier. Its revenue rose 52.5% to Rs 865.6 crore. The company’s EBITDA rose 54.1% to Rs 135.6 crore from Rs 88 crore a year ago, while EBITDA margin expanded 20 basis points to 15.7%. NALCO National Aluminium Company Ltd (NALCO) reported a 28% year-on-year rise in standalone profit after tax to Rs 1,835 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 1,433 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue from operations increased 26.3% to Rs 5,419.4 crore from Rs 4,292.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Higher earnings from its aluminium business helped offset the decline in its chemicals segment. docs.title: iPhone Air 2 with dual cameras – What industry analyst say about Apple’s thinnest phone
docs.text: The iPhone Air was a breath of fresh air in the premium smartphone world. At a time when everyone is focused on stuffing the largest batteries and the most cameras, the Air was simply a slim phone. Despite being the thinnest, the Air did not suffer from the Bendgate controversy that plagues the iPhone 6 from a decade ago. However, that sleek silhouette came with noticeable compromises – a single rear camera, a scaled-down battery, and thermal limits that constrained top-tier performance. Now, a host of supply-chain reports and industry leaks suggest Apple is preparing a second-generation model that directly addresses those pain points. The rumoured iPhone Air 2 aims to bridge the gap between design-forward minimalism and power-user functionality. iPhone Air 2: Doubling down on cameras The most significant physical change coming to the iPhone Air 2 is on the back. Industry analysts, including GF Securities' Jeff Pu, point to a new dual-camera setup featuring a 48 MP main sensor alongside a second 48 MP Ultra Wide lens. Pu says that adding a second lens without thickening up the total device thickness has forced a cosmetic rethink. Early CAD renders and leaks indicate Apple may adopt a wider, horizontal pill-shaped bump reminiscent of Google's recent Pixel camera visors, housing both sensors cleanly in a single module. ALSO READTop 6 air purifiers to buy under Rs 30,000 to beat winter pollution Even thinner yet more power inside Despite incorporating a secondary camera and a larger battery, leakers like Korean blogger “yeux1122” and Weibo's “Digital Chat Station” report that Apple plans to trim the chassis down from 5.6 mm to a mere 5.2 mm. To make room inside such an enclosure, Apple is reportedly leveraging two crucial architectural changes: Colour Filter on Encapsulation (CoE) OLED displays: A Samsung-developed display assembly that strips away polarizing layers to yield a thinner screen panel. 2-Nanometer A20 Pro chipset: Moving to TSMC’s 2nm node offers dramatic power efficiency gains. This efficiency allows a reported 3,500 mAh battery (~11% capacity bump) to deliver significantly longer runtime without adding physical bulk. To keep heat under control within the wafer-thin frame, supply-chain sources, like Ming-Chi Kuo (TF International Securities) and Pu, report that Apple is embedding a thin vapour chamber cooling system—hardware previously seen in ultra-thin foldable designs. iPhone Air 2 launch window and expected price in India Unlike standard flagship iPhones that launch every September, current forecasts suggest that Apple is slating the iPhone Air 2 for a Spring launch window, alongside the baseline iPhone 18 series. While early global pricing leaks suggest it will target the $1,099 range, Indian consumers can expect local pricing to reflect import duties and taxes. Current iPhone Air (First-Gen) base price in India: Rs 1,19,900 (256GB base variant). Estimated iPhone Air 2 price in India: Given the added dual-camera hardware, 2nm chipset, and upgraded thermal architecture, industry expectations place the baseline 256GB variant of the iPhone Air 2 between Rs 1,24,900 and Rs 1,29,900 in India at launch. If these leaks and pricing expectations prove accurate, the iPhone Air 2 won't just be an engineering showcase—it will be a far more practical choice for daily driver duties. docs.title: SECL IPO: From 26-year reserves to 91% profit jump, 5 must-know details about Coal India arm
docs.text: Every time a light switches on in an Indian home, there is a fair chance that coal from a single corner of Chhattisgarh helped make it happen. South Eastern Coalfields (SECL) digs out about one of every six tonnes of coal the country burns and runs two of the largest mines on Earth. Yet if you own Coal India shares, you already hold a piece of it without ever seeing its name on your screen. South Eastern Coalfields, a subsidiary of Coal India, has filed its draft papers with the market regulator. Here are five key things investors should know about the proposed IPO. Coal India is selling shares, not raising fresh capital SECL's proposed IPO will comprise an offer for sale of up to 66.80 crore equity shares by its promoter, Coal India. Each share has a face value of Rs 2. Since the issue is entirely an OFS, the proceeds from the share sale will go to the selling shareholder, Coal India, rather than SECL. The company will not receive fresh funds through the offering. ALSO READJio Platforms financials: Telecom arm draws 87% revenue; rising debt costs signal caution The IPO will follow the book-building process. Under the proposed allocation structure, up to 50% of the net offer will be reserved for qualified institutional buyers, while non-institutional investors and retail investors will have allocations of up to 15% and 35%, respectively. How big is SECL's coal business? SECL was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh. It is a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India and holds Miniratna Category-I status. It is also the second-largest coal producer among Coal India's subsidiaries, contributing 22.95% of the parent company's production. Its output increased 5.25% from 167.49 million tonnes in FY25. According to the company's DRHP, this was the highest production growth among Coal India's subsidiaries during the period. Nearly 26 years of reserves: What does the resource base look like? Coal availability is an important factor for a mining company's long-term operations. SECL had total geological coal resources of approximately 47.55 billion tonnes as of April 1, 2026. Its audited coal reserves stood at 4.61 billion tonnes. Based on its FY26 production of 176.29 million tonnes, the company estimates that these audited reserves could support production for approximately 26 years. Its Gevra and Kusmunda mines in Chhattisgarh's Korba coalfield are also among the world's largest coal mines by production capacity. The company has 53 producing mines, including 19 opencast and 34 underground mines Revenue and profit: How did the company perform? SECL reported revenue from operations of Rs 16,593.7 crore for the six months ended September 30, 2026, compared with Rs 15,090.2 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier. ALSO READ10 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Motilal Oswal with 21% to 68% upside potential Its net profit increased to Rs 2,174.3 crore from Rs 1,140.9 crore during the same period. For FY26, revenue from operations stood at Rs 32,956.5 crore, against Rs 29,998.3 crore in FY25. Net profit increased to Rs 4,754.5 crore from Rs 4,540.4 crore. How does SECL transport its coal? Mining coal is only one part of the business. Moving it from mines to power plants and other customers is equally important. SECL uses railway connectivity through the South East Central Railway zone, along with dedicated Merry-Go-Round (MGR) systems and belt conveyors. Road transportation is another important channel. Who are the IPO managers? SBI Capital Markets, ICICI Securities, IDBI Capital Markets and Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors are the book-running lead managers. KFin Technologies has been appointed registrar to the issue. The shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE). Disclaimer: This article provides factual analysis only and is not, and should not be construed as, an offer, solicitation, or recommendation to buy or sell securities. Investors must conduct their own independent due diligence and seek advice from a SEBI-registered financial advisor.

docs.title: EAAA India Alternatives lists at a slight premium; surges nearly 3% intra-day
docs.text: The shares of EAAA India Alternatives debuted at Rs 1,673 apiece on the BSE on Monday, November 2. This reflects a premium of a mere 0.5% from its issue price of Rs 1,665. The shares rose 2.7% to a high of Rs 1,711 apiece just minutes after listing. Here is a look at the key details of the issues – ALSO READMK Sons Fine Jewels IPO Opens: Check price band, lot size of Rs 275 cr issue EAAA India Alternatives: Business fundamentals, issue details The public issue of EAAA India Alternatives was open for subscription from October 26 to October 28. The issue was subscribed 5.25 times as on the final day, with strong demand from qualified institutional buyers (QIBs). The portion reserved for QIBs was subscribed 13.13 times while the non-institutional investors (NII) portion was subscribed 4.58 times. The retail investor portion was subscribed 1.03 times. The initial public offering (IPO) was solely an offer for sale. Under the issue, the company’s promoter group, Edelweiss Securities and Investments Private Limited, planned to offload 72.07 lakh shares to raise Rs 1,200 crore. The company will receive no proceeds through the issue. The price band of the offer was fixed at RS 1,585 to Rs 1,665 per share. Ahead of its opening, EAAA India Alternatives had raised Rs 360 crore from anchor investors. The anchor book included Goldman Sachs, BNP Paribas Financial Markets, Hornbill Capital Advisors, and Schroder International. ALSO READJio Platforms financials: Telecom arm draws 87% revenue; rising debt costs signal caution The IPO was handled by Axis Capital, Jefferies India, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, and Nuvama Wealth Management. MUFG Intime India was appointed as the registrar for the offer.

 GOCOLORS 
 Motilal Oswal's research report on Go Fashion India

Pre-Ind AS EBITDA (ex-one-offs) declined 40% YoY to INR200m in 2Q, with margin contracting 570bp YoY to 9.2%, as RM pressure (~180bp) from fabric inflation and higher brand investments weighed on profitability. Buy V Guard Industries; target of Rs 420: Anand Rathi
 VGUARD 
 Anand Rathi's research report on V Guard Industries 
 A 31.2% EBITDA beat was driven by broad-based growth and tighter SG&A, offsetting RM cost pressures. V-Guard continues to outgrow the industry, led by its Electronics portfolio (stabilizers, inverters, batteries and solar panels) and price-led growth in wires. We expect demand momentum to sustain in FY27, driven by continued strength in Electronics & Electricals and recovery in ECD and Sunflame, supporting 13.9% revenue CAGR over FY26-29E (~2-3% ahead of industry growth). We forecast 23.3% PAT CAGR over FY26-29E, with ~160bps margin expansion, aided by Sunflame synergies and recovery in Consumer Durables. Strong brand equity, expanding distribution, rising in-house manufacturing mix and experienced leadership should support growth and profitability. Low capex intensity and healthy cash generation should drive ~510bps RoCE expansion to 22.1% by FY29e. 
 Outlook

 WPIL 
 Emkay Global Financial' research report on WPIL 
 WPIL reported a weak 2QFY27 performance with a miss on our expectations – consolidated revenue/EBITDA came in at Rs3.5bn/Rs472mn, declining 17%/41% yoy. EBITDA margin declined by 550bps yoy at 13.3%. Products revenue at Rs2.1bn (-14.7% yoy) and Projects revenue at Rs1.4bn (-19.9% yoy). The subdued performance in the products division was due to deferral of large orders which is expected to normalize in 2H. Projects division saw lumpiness in revenue booking on the international front and slower execution of JJM orders on the domestic front. Order backlog at end-2QFY27 stands at Rs51bn (47:53 mix between domestic and international).  NAVINFLUOR 
 Anand Rathi's research report on Navin Fluorine International 
 Navin Fluorine International (NFIL) Q2FY27 EBITDA stood at Rs4.1bn, ~10%/15% above our/consensus est. driven by: (a) ~57% y/y and 14% q/q revenue growth across HPP (up 50% y/y), Specialty Chemicals (up 58% y/y) and CDMO (up 78% y/y); (b) steady EBITDA margin of 34.2% (up 176bps y/y) with stable gross margin q/q absorbing RM inflation via pricing, forex tailwinds and efficiency.
